While existing TAI studies mainly focus on idealized systems such as discrete lattice models or resonator arrays, here we realize the disorder‐engineering principle in a scalable continuous elastic plate for topological states and waveguide‐cavity critical couplings. Disorder is introduced by randomly rotating perforated elliptical holes in a continuous plate. The disorder‐assisted bandgap closing and reopening, and interface states with suppressed backscattering, are verified experimentally. We also develop a super‐periodic equivalent model that quantitatively predicts the disorder‐driven bandgap evolutions and topological transitions. Beyond robust transport, we realize disorder‐assisted critical couplings in a TAI waveguide‐cavity system, whereby most waveguide energy is coupled into the resonator, with possible applications in signal filtering and multiplexing. Our work introduces a disorder‐engineering strategy for manipulating wave phenomena in continuous solid‐state media. We expect these results to inspire further advances in integrated phononic circuits and on‐chip technologies.
nb66575debb22: Adaptive manipulation of vectorial optical fields is important for optical metrology, imaging, and structured light‐related applications, yet existing approaches often rely on bulky or sequentially operated systems. Here we demonstrate an inkjet‐printed negative dielectric anisotropy nematic liquid crystal droplet platform that unifies adaptive complex beam generation and full‐vectorial optical field sensing within a single printed architecture. For complex beam generation, electric‐field‐driven director reconfiguration in the droplets produces tunable birefringence and wavelength‐dependent polarization textures, including skyrmionic‐like optical fields. For adaptive full‐vectorial optical field sensing, the same droplet array enables spectral and polarization retrieval through wavelength‐dependent intensity patterns and division‐of‐wavefront polarimetry, while also functioning as a microlens array for Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensing to reconstruct phase. These results establish negative dielectric anisotropy liquid crystal droplets as a scalable soft‐matter photonic system for adaptive beam manipulation and multidimensional optical field characterization.
n0bffc7007eca: Composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) hold immense promise for high‐energy‐density solid‐state lithium metal batteries, yet their practical application remains severely hampered by filler agglomeration and sluggish interfacial Li+ transport. Herein, dual‐functional supramolecular bridging networks are constructed by employing lithiated carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC‐Li) as dynamic bridges to interconnect polydopamine (PDA)‐modified Li6.28Al0.24La3Zr2O12 (LLZAO) fillers within a PVDF‐HFP matrix. This synergistic architecture helps promote a more uniform filler dispersion and actively mediates ion solvation dynamics via simultaneous anion trapping and cation extraction. Crucially, this dual‐regulation fundamentally mitigates the space‐charge layer (SCL) effect at organic‐inorganic boundaries, actively unlocking a highly efficient trans‐phase Li+ percolation pathway through the LLZAO ceramic bulk, thereby bypassing conventionally sluggish interfacial routes. The resulting spatially homogeneous ion flux may reduce localized current hotspots and suppress lithium dendrite proliferation. Consequently, the optimized PVPL electrolyte empowers Li||Li symmetrical cells to maintain stable plating/stripping over 1400 h. Furthermore, LiFePO4||PVPL||Li full cells deliver 83% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 2 C, while NCM811||PVPL||Li cells maintain 88% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This dual‐functional bridging strategy establishes a generalizable and effective paradigm for engineering advanced CSEs with optimized structural and Li+ transport kinetics.
nf49b2b91c1ac: Despite the effectiveness of surface passivation, simultaneous optimization of buried interface and top surface in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains challenging due to incompatible additive functions and uncontrolled crystallization kinetics. Here, we present a dual‐interface regulation strategy that deploys phenyltrimethylammonium chloride (THPA) treatment on the top surface and 5‐amino‐1‐pentanol (5‐APT) treatment at the buried interface of the perovskite film. This approach achieves multiple collaborative regulation effects of dual interfaces: (i) THPA reduces trap density at the top surface of perovskites and promotes n‐type character. (ii) 5‐APT forms hydrogen and ionic bonds with the substrate, enhancing bottom crystallinity via cation exchange with FA+/Cs+ and facilitating hole extraction. Besides, in‐situ photoluminescence reveals that 5‐APT retards the crystallization process, promoting grain merging and yielding uniformly sized grains. As a result, the optimized PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24% with excellent stability. This straightforward strategy transcends conventional spacer cation engineering, bridging the efficiency‐stability divide and providing a generalizable paradigm for interface passivation in perovskite optoelectronics.
n3fee539fceab: The inherent trade‐offs among processability, wet stability, and environmental footprint of biomass‐derived materials hinder the development of sustainable alternatives to petroleum‐based plastics. Here, we report an ambient‐solvent‐regulated strategy that transforms native cellulose paper into a robust, weldable, and rapidly biodegradable plastic using a ternary iron(III) chloride/zinc chloride/water (FeCl3/ZnCl2/H2O) molten salt hydrate system. Leveraging the small ionic radius and high charge density of Fe3+, this system achieves rapid, ambient‐temperature partial dissolution of cellulose rather than full homogeneous disassembly, preserving the native microfiber skeleton while Fe3+ ions serve as permanent yet dynamic molecular rivets within the regenerated matrix during in situ reconstruction. The resulting Fe3+‐enhanced multiscale cellulose paper delivers 41.6 MPa dry tensile strength and 11.2 MPa wet strength. Dynamic Fe3+–O coordination bonds enable vitrimer‐like water‐assisted welding and binder‐free straw fabrication. Notably, the solvent remains effective over ten reuse cycles, with 75% strength retention. Life cycle assessment reveals a global warming potential of 1.82 kg CO2‐eq/kg, 40% and 21% lower than polylactic acid and polyethylene, respectively. Furthermore, the integrated Fe3+ centers trigger Fenton‐like self‐destruction in soil, achieving complete degradation within 35 days. This work establishes a coordination mechanochemistry strategy for designing high‐performance bioplastics with closed‐loop life cycles.
ndffbb8e6881d: The calendar life of lithium (Li) metal batteries is commonly evaluated through cycling performance, implicitly assuming that storage-induced degradation follows the same interfacial processes. However, this work reveals that Li metal undergoes continuous non-Faradaic interfacial corrosion under open-circuit conditions, defining a distinct degradation pathway governing calendar aging, distinct from cycling-induced failure. To quantify this process, we introduce a kinetically defined descriptor based on the degradation rate constant (λ), enabling direct evaluation of time-dependent capacity loss during storage. This framework treats calendar aging as a corrosion-driven kinetic process rather than an extrapolation of cycling behavior. We further show that static corrosion can be actively regulated via electrolyte design. Based on the degradation rate constants derived from capacity decay fitting, the LiNO3-15C5-CsBr electrolyte projects a 2.7-fold extension in storage lifetime at 100% SOC and a 3.4-fold extension at 0% SOC versus the baseline electrolyte. Mechanistically, Cs+-mediated electrostatic shielding, Br−-induced interfacial polishing, and NO3 −-derived inorganic passivation cooperatively stabilize the Li interface, suppress corrosion kinetics, and reduce irreversible Li loss, leading to a marked decrease in λ. These findings establish static corrosion as a distinct degradation mode in Li metal batteries and provide a quantitative framework for evaluating and regulating calendar aging beyond cycling metrics.
nddad5430a75b: Aqueous zinc batteries are plagued by dendrite growth and parasitic reactions, calling for a rational interfacial design. Herein, we construct a core–shell ZIF-8@SiO2 architecture on the Zn anode (ZFSI@Zn) via a self-nucleation route. The hydrophilic SiO2 shell and anion-affinitive ZIF-8 core synergistically facilitate Zn2+ desolvation and transport, enhancing the 3D diffusion contribution while effectively suppressing interfacial concentration polarization. Consequently, the ZFSI@Zn anode delivers an extended lifespan of 1800 h at 1 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2 and maintains remarkable stability even at an ultrahigh current density of 50 mA cm−2. Beyond anode protection, strong SO4 2− adsorption confers a negative surface charge that electrostatically repels I3 −, thereby eliminating the shuttle effect in Zn-I2 batteries. This enables a maximum specific capacity of 202.3 mAh g−1 at 0.2 A g−1 and an outstanding capacity retention of 89.8% over 65 000 cycles at 5 A g−1, corresponding to an ultralow capacity decay of merely 0.00015% per cycle. The superior performance is further validated under high cathode loadings and in pouch‑cell configurations. Overall, this work establishes core–shell interfacial engineering as a versatile platform for tackling the multiple challenges in zinc‑based energy storage.
n3026886c0bb9: As a turnover technology capable of painlessly breaching the transdermal barrier, microneedles (MNs) have overcome the limitations of solitary transdermal drug delivery, progressively evolving into highly integrated theranostic platforms. Tracing the evolution of bio‐interfacial mass transfer and systemic integration, this review systematically categorizes MN architectures into solid, hollow, coated, dissolving, hydrogel, and layered types, highlighting the critical roles of micromolding, high‐resolution lithography, and three‐dimensional printing in the precise fabrication of MN arrays. In alignment with this technological trend, this review systematically delineates two core trajectories of MN functional evolution and provides an in‐depth discussion on intervention strategies that overcome complex pathological microenvironments to achieve precise targeted drug delivery, while analyzing their sensing potential in situ extraction of dermal interstitial fluid and dynamic monitoring of biochemical biomarkers. Finally, the review explores the manufacturing and production barriers hindering the bench‐to‐bedside clinical translation of MN systems and envisions their promising future evolution toward intelligent closed‐loop theranostic platforms integrating sensing, decision‐making, and therapeutics. Ultimately, an overarching research framework for the MN field that combines systemic comprehensiveness, broad applicability, and introductory guidance is established.
n66128e9bf9c2: The advantage of dual‐carriers heterostructures has expanded the functional boundaries of semiconductor devices in bidirectional control, logical operations, high‐frequency communication, and precision medicine, which stand as a cornerstone for development of next‐generation information technologies and renewable energy systems. The excitation of dual‐carriers is usually realized in semiconductor heterostructures but suffers a significant challenge in real applications because of complex interface design and band structure modulation limitations. The dual‐carriers excitation in metallic heterostructures is strongly expected. In this work, we realized dual‐carriers excitation in a metallic transport van der Waals heterostructure. Compared with the single‐layer film, the heterostructure sample exhibits a pronounced nonlinear ordinary Hall curve. This transport phenomenon provides key material support for core technologies in fields such as electronic information, energy conversion, and optoelectronics.
nfc82f683dd2d: Lithium oxygen batteries hold great promise as high‐energy‐density storage technologies, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish cathode redox kinetics. A key bottleneck lies in the inefficient electron transfer associated with the formation and decomposition of the LiO2 intermediate, which leads to severe polarization and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose a facet‐induced electron‐bridge engineering to boost LiO2‐mediated reaction kinetics. By harnessing a Mott–Schottky built‐in electric field across the heterointerface, we drive directional charge separation that simultaneously tailors electron density and sorption microenvironments. The resulting intermediate‐binding energetics reprogram the reaction trajectory, affording precise manipulation over Li2O2 nucleation kinetics and the subsequent pathways governing its growth and decomposition. Consequently, the engineered cathode thus delivers extended cycle life with a substantially reduced overpotential. This work provides a general principle for regulating reaction intermediates and accelerating electron transfer via crystal plane optimization and interfacial engineering, offering a reliable strategy for high‐performance electrocatalysts.
nf20ea3302d06: Heterostructure materials have garnered substantial interest across optics, medicine, optoelectronics, and electromagnetics due to their ability to combine advantageous characteristics from multiple constituent phases. Notably, Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions have demonstrated enhancement mechanisms for both photogenerated charge carrier separation and nonlinear optical response. However, their optoelectronic properties from a theoretical perspective and their potential in ultrafast photonics have not been extensively explored. Herein, robust S─O covalent‐bonded Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions were successfully synthesized via heat treatment technology. First‐principles calculations were conducted to examine thermal stability, electronic band structures, density of states distributions, electron localization functions, and dielectric responses, thereby establishing a fundamental understanding of intrinsic material properties while informing future optoelectronic implementations. By employing the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction in a fiber cavity with negative dispersion, passive mode‐locking operation was realized, delivering a pulse width of 300 fs. Moreover, the incorporation of the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction into a net positive dispersion fiber cavity resulted in the achievement of mode‐locked operation with a pulse duration of 123 fs. Compared with previous studies, these lasers show improved performance. This work advances the understanding of Fe2O3/In2S3 structure‐property relationships from a theoretical perspective and highlights their potential as promising nonlinear optical materials for advanced optoelectronic devices from an experimental standpoint.
n52d3918b966b: Substrate clamping constrains lattice deformation in epitaxial ferroelectrics, limiting the ability of weak non‐electrical stimuli to reconfigure polarization. Here, we show that releasing epitaxial PbTiO3 into a freestanding membrane reshapes its switching landscape and enables polarization control through electrical, mechanical, and optical stimuli. Whereas substrate‐clamped PbTiO3 remains stable under local mechanical loading up to 4000 nN and 405‐nm illumination, freestanding PbTiO3 integrated on silicon exhibits force‐driven polarization reconfiguration from ∼2000 nN and pronounced light‐assisted modification of the written polar state. Mechanical release enhances the piezoresponse by ∼80%, reduces the switching voltage by ∼45%, and produces a strongly force‐tunable electromechanical response. Optical excitation further induces asymmetric switching and a positive hysteresis shift in the freestanding membrane, consistent with a photoinduced internal bias field. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals photoinduced surface‐potential modulation in both clamped and freestanding geometries, yet corresponding polarization reconfiguration occurs only in the mechanically released membrane. This contrast demonstrates that photoinduced electrostatic perturbation alone is insufficient to drive polarization reconfiguration and that its effectiveness is governed by the mechanical boundary condition. Our findings establish mechanical release as a strategy for engineering the accessibility of ferroelectric switching pathways and enabling multi‐stimulus control in reconfigurable oxide membranes.
n38e91a875906: Solid‐state lithium batteries (SSLBs) are promising next‐generation energy storage devices, but their widespread deployment is largely hampered by costly, resource‐intensive solid electrolytes. Here we report a low‐cost, high‐performance, and sustainable solid composite electrolyte (SCE) membrane that comprises commercial high‐alkali glass fiber (GF) separators as scaffolds for in situ polymerization of the PEGDA/LiTFSI/FEC matrix. The alkali‐doped silicate framework in GF provides abundant Lewis acid‐base sites that promote lithium salt dissociation and enhance directional Li+ transport. The resulting GF‐SCE exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.89 × 10−4 S cm−1 at 25°C, a wide electrochemical stability window up to 5.0 V, and extensive dendrite‐free cycling, enabling the formation of a stable LiF‐rich solid‐electrolyte interphase. When GF‐SCE is used in a cell containing high‐Ni LiNi0.96Co0.03Mn0.01O2 cathode and Li metal anode, a large specific capacity of 253.6 mAh g−1 and stable cycling are achieved. Techno‐economic analyses show that the production cost of GF‐SCE membranes is only $8.98–$17.15 m−2 via solvent‐free roll‐to‐roll processing with earth‐abundant precursors, favorably competitive relative to other inorganic electrolyte counterparts. By combining high electrochemical performance, potential scalability, and favorable recyclability, the glass‐fiber‐based SCEs reported in this work offer a practical, cost‐effective pathway toward circular and high‐voltage solid‐state lithium batteries.
n3261d59911f9: High‐Alkali Glass Fiber Composite Electrolytes Waste glass fiber becomes an active electrolyte scaffold: alkali‐rich silicate surfaces dissociate lithium salts and steer directional Li+ transport. The solid composite membrane cycles dendrite‐free at high voltage, offering a low‐cost route to sustainable solid‐state lithium batteries. More details can be found in the Research Article Dong Shu, Lei Zhang, Lifeng Liu, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77793).
nf4ce47223c9f: The controlled and scalable fabrication of multimetal metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging due to differences in metal coordination kinetics and complex crystal evolution. Herein, a graphene oxide (GO)‐assisted one‐pot strategy is developed to prepare an accordion‐like NiCoFeCuZn‐MOF/GO composite assembled from single‐crystalline MOF nanosheets. Stepwise introduction of Ni, Co, Fe, Cu, and Zn into the BDC‐based MOF/GO platform (BDC = 1,4‐benzenedicarboxylic acid) reveals structural evolution. Tracking the growth process shows that GO promotes heterogeneous nucleation and multimetal incorporation. GO‐guided growth and the inherent two‐dimensional tendency of the Ni‐BDC framework facilitate layered structure formation. DFT calculations and compositional modulation indicate that unfavorable Cu/Zn substitution at exposed surface sites limits complete exfoliation during anti‐ripening, preserving partial interlayer contact and leading to the accordion‐like structure. The strategy enables kilogram‐scale preparation with preserved accordion‐like morphology and extends to NDC‐ and BPDC‐based systems (NDC = 2,6‐naphthalenedicarboxylic acid, BPDC = 4,4′‐biphenyldicarboxylic acid), demonstrating its generality. NiCoFeCuZn‐MOF/GO delivers 223.3 mA h g−1 at 1 mA cm−2 in a quasi‐solid‐state zinc battery and requires an overpotential of 213 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 for the OER. These findings provide guidance for controlled growth of multimetal MOF/GO composites for electrochemical energy storage and conversion.
n20a4a60fc43e: High‐capacity and long‐lifespan anode materials are essential to advance the practical deployment of sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). Transition metal sulfides are promising anode candidates due to their high theoretical capacity, yet their practical applications are hindered by cycling‐induced volume expansion, inferior conductivity, and sodium polysulfide shuttling. This work constructs a novel composite material by embedding ZnS/SnS2 heterojunctions into nitrogen‐doped porous glucose‐derived hard carbon (H‐ZSS/NC‐950P) to solve these drawbacks. Electrochemical tests confirm the optimized material delivers outstanding sodium storage performance. It retains a reversible capacity of 588.1 mAh·g−1 after 300 cycles at 1.0 A·g−1, maintains 395.8 mAh·g−1 at an ultrahigh current of 50 A·g−1, and achieves 68% capacity retention over 6000 cycles at 10 A·g−1. Such superior performance stems from synergistic effects of the heterostructure. The ZnS/SnS2 heterointerface builds an internal electric field to boost charge transfer. Nitrogen doping promotes surface pseudocapacitance. The porous carbon matrix accelerates ion diffusion, relieves volume strain, and anchors sodium polysulfides. Combined with CV and in situ XRD results, a conversion‐alloying sodium storage mechanism is verified. Full‐cell tests with a Na3V2(PO4)3 cathode further prove its practical feasibility. This research clarifies the storage mechanism of metal sulfide‐carbon heterostructures and offers a reliable strategy for high‐performance SIBs anode development.
n5fa11163b786: In this study, for the first time, the digital light processing (DLP) based 3D printing of graded metallopolymer structures is presented. Herein, the individual segments are based on the combination of terpyridine‐ and triphenylmethyl(trt)‐histidine‐based monomers crosslinked with zinc(II) and nickel(II) salts, respectively. Subsequently, photopolymerization with 2‐phenoxyethyl acrylate as a comonomer is conducted using the same printing conditions for all mixtures. At defined times, the resin mixtures are exchanged, leading to graded structures. Prior to this study, it was not possible to access such graded materials based on the segmented combination of chemically different metal complexes. Temperature‐dependent Raman spectroscopy is utilized to investigate the materials with a special focus on the interface between the different segments. Here, a narrow dynamic region at the intersection, thinner than one printing layer (about 20 µm), was detected. The implemented metal‐ligand combinations can be thermally activated and enable excellent shape‐memory abilities, without the need for switching via the glass transition temperature. Furthermore, the permanent shape can be recovered in two steps, and thermo‐mechanical analysis measurements revealed excellent shape fixities (close to 100%) and overall recovery rates (as high as 99%).
n2cbb61124b08: Intelligent hydrogel actuators with self‐sensing capabilities have shown broad prospects in flexible electronics, bioinspired robotics, and human–machine interaction. However, most reported self‐sensing hydrogel actuators still suffer from insufficient sensing sensitivity and low efficiency in structural‐response coupling, which restrict their application in highly integrated self‐sensing systems. Here, we develop a high‐sensitivity self‐sensing actuating hydrogel through embedding micro‐nano collaborative island‐bridge conductive network of liquid metal (LM) and carbon nanotube (CNT) within thermal‐responsive poly(N‐isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) matrix, allowing external strain and photothermal actuation to be translated into amplified electrical signals through reversible fracture and reconstruction of conductive pathways. The as‐prepared hydrogel exhibits ultrahigh strain sensitivity (Gauge Factor = 38.9) and precise actuation self‐sensing capability (ΔR/R0 > 200%). Benefiting from the excellent sensing performance, the proposed LM/CNT‐PNIPAM (LCP) self‐sensing hydrogel not only enables high‐fidelity monitoring of human motion and physiological signals in wearable electronics, but also exhibits potential as gesture‐controlled remote navigation of intelligent vehicle by integrating with machine‐learning algorithm. Moreover, through combining with IoT communication technique, a bioinspired self‐sensing tentacle with high‐accuracy recognition capacity was developed based on the excellent self‐sensing feature of the LCP hydrogel. This study lays a material foundation for developing intelligent soft systems with accurate feedback regulation and further human–machine interaction capacity.
n42944086095a: Lithium extraction from brines is limited by severe ion interference and interior performance of conventional separation technologies. Existing solar evaporators also suffer from insufficient salt resistance, low mass transfer efficiency and poor lithium selectivity, which restricts the simultaneous high‐efficiency production of freshwater and lithium recovery. Herein, a hollow cage‐like dynamic evaporator @ACRC–10 is fabricated. Its hollow structure optimizes vapor diffusion in large‐scale evaporation. The elliptical bearing enables radiant light regulation and interfacial thermal management, and the curved structure achieves directional water transport and localized salt crystallization. Driven by salt crystal gravity, the evaporator realizes autonomous salt shedding, active self‐cleaning, and efficient salt resource utilization. Outdoor tests demonstrate an evaporation rate of 2.48 kg m−2 h−1, a lithium adsorption capacity of 65.62 mg g−1, a Li/Mg separation factor of 139.61, and a steady daily water yield of 25 L m−2 over 32 days of continuous operation. This integrated system addresses the single functional drawbacks of conventional technologies, providing an effective strategy for green lithium extraction and freshwater recovery from brine.
ncbbec23e8199: Epithelial tissue integrity and remodeling rely on mechanical coupling between cytoskeletal organization and adhesion complexes, but their orchestration in three‐dimensional (3D) epithelia remains unresolved. Here, we introduced a noninvasive strategy to locally probe forces within 3D epithelial tissues. We engineered elastic polyacrylamide (PAAm) microbeads with cell‐like size and mechanical properties, enabling their integration into tissues. PAAm microbeads were spontaneously engulfed by the tissue, establishing an intrinsic interface. This allowed bead deformation to be directly correlated with local cytoskeletal architecture and adhesion organization, visualized through high‐resolution imaging and quantitative 3D computational reconstruction. Using this approach, we demonstrated that localized mechanical perturbations trigger cytoskeletal remodeling while preserving tissue polarity. We further identified extracellular matrix composition as a key determinant of bead‐tissue interactions. At the bead–cell interface, cells assembled tension‐bearing focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. Quantitative analysis of bead deformation revealed sub‐cellular scale patterns of cell‐bead interaction forces, which correlated with the localization of cytoskeletal elements. Our findings extend previous traction force microscopy observations to 3D, revealing coordinated, spatially heterogeneous forces specifically at the cell–bead interface. Taken together, this enabled us to dissect the interplay between cellular processes and tissue mechanics in a noninvasive way in 3D model systems.
n4346bfb6baa5: Biological signals are inherently weak and susceptible to noise, making in situ signal amplification critical for high-fidelity sensing. Electronic fibers offer unique advantages for conformal and scalable biointegration; however, fiber amplifiers are seldom reported due to the lack of suitable semiconducting materials that combine balanced ambipolar transport, scalable fiber fabrication, and high device performance. Herein, we report the first single-component ambipolar fiber platform based on a newly designed polymer, P(gTDPP-TQ), which combines balanced p- and n-type transport, low-cost synthesis, and continuous fiber fabrication. Fiber processing enhances molecular ordering and charge transport, yielding record-high µC* and g m,norm among reported semiconducting fibers, enabling high-performance fiber amplifiers with a high voltage gain of up to 150 V V−1 and low operating voltages down to 0.5 V. These fiber amplifiers enable high-fidelity electroencephalogram signal amplification over 20 times and sensitive cortisol sensing with a record-low detection limit of 3.7 fM. This work establishes a general ambipolar fiber platform for integrated bioelectronic amplification and sensing.
n46af3b44a21f: During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu2SnSe3‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd2+ partially substitutes Zn2+ sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.
n7b8328bdd9db: Thermal runaway in lithium‐ion batteries often develops from a local failure into a spatially propagating high‐temperature front. Here, we show that oxygen‐bearing cathode materials and metallic aluminium can form self‐sustained, glowing, cathode‐driven aluminothermic fronts in inert gas as a heat‐amplification pathway relevant to severe thermal runaway. Using a mesoscale platform based on semi‐1D composite bars, we isolate this interfacial redox chemistry from gas‐phase combustion, internal short‐circuit heating, and other coupled cell‐failure processes. Nickel‐rich layered oxide/aluminium bars sustain aluminothermic‐front propagation in argon, with velocities of the same order of magnitude as reported thermal‐runaway fronts. By varying aluminium loading, reaction atmosphere and cathode chemistry, we show that front propagation depends on aluminium fuel supply, the oxygen‐donor capability of the cathode, and access to oxygen gas. Crystalline phase and chemical‐state analyses reveal Li–Al–O/Al–O products together with reduced or reconstructed transition‐metal species, supporting cathode‐to‐aluminium oxygen transfer as the underlying redox pathway. For a representative 2‐Ah cell, energy‐audit calculations indicate that the aluminium‐cathode reaction gives a potential heat scale equivalent to about half of the stored electrical energy. These findings identify cathode‐Al redox chemistry as an internal heat‐amplification mechanism that should be considered in battery hazard assessment and high‐energy‐cell safety design.
n14085b0ffc7c: Zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next‐generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. However, their commercialization is severely hindered by poor cycle stability, primarily originating from dendritic Zn growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution. To address these challenges simultaneously, we design and integrate a multifunctional polymeric protective layer incorporating amide and imidazolium functional groups. The zincophilic amide groups facilitate ion transport by providing stable Zn2+ binding sites, whereas the hygroscopic imidazolium groups establish a confined‐water domain that regulates local solvation dynamics. Within this domain, water molecules transiently stabilize Zn2+ and act as a coordination bridge during ion migration, yet their mobility toward the electrode surface is restricted. This dual functionality increases the Zn2+ single‐ion conductivity 6.55‐fold and reduces the hydrogen evolution rate by 79.1%. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit markedly extended cycling lifetimes of up to 2200 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. When applied to Zn–I2 full cells, the protective layer enables stable operation over 4000 cycles with >85% capacity retention, even under a practical areal capacity of 3.6 mAh cm−2. These findings highlight a robust interfacial strategy to realize long‐duration, high‐capacity aqueous ZIBs for grid‐scale energy storage.
nb645cf934be7: Compression-torsion metamaterials (CTMs) that break spatial inversion symmetry face persistent trade-offs among large deformation capacity, intrinsic stiffness, and fatigue durability. Crucially, boundary rotation induced by axial compression complicates integration with rotationally constrained engineering interfaces. Here we introduce a chiral three-rod tensegrity cell (CTTC) paradigm that addresses these conflicts through a cross-scale dual-decoupling strategy. First, mechanical decoupling at the unit-cell scale separates macroscopic shape-morphing from large local material strain: a heterogeneous rigid-flexible architecture channels global compression into kinematic rod displacement and uniform elastic-network stretching, achieving 97° torsion at Level 0 and only 4.87% peak-force degradation over 10 000 cycles at Level 3. An integrated geometric interlocking reconfigurator further enables post-fabrication programmability of stiffness and strain-normalized twist ratio (R T-S). Second, kinematic decoupling at the assembly scale localizes torsional deformation as a boundary-decoupled internal rotational mode, while maintaining external interfaces in pure translation. This cross-scale framework establishes a deployable paradigm bridging metamaterial physics and robotic systems operating in geometrically constrained environments.
nb1c9c4fb8713: The electrochemical CO2 and CO reduction (COxRR) to value‐added multicarbon (C2+) products offers a promising route for sustainable carbon recycling and renewable fuel generation. Although Cu catalysts exhibit unique activity, these single‐metal sites are constrained by linear scaling relations of intermediate adsorption energies, which limits further improvements in selectivity and energy efficiency. Introducing heteroatoms to regulate active‐site coordination provides an effective approach to transcend these limitations. This review describes recent advances in the theoretical design, controllable fabrication, and mechanistic investigation of heteroatomic active sites for COxRR toward C2+ products. Theoretical identification for high‐performance sites through descriptor‐based modeling, data‐driven screening, and dynamic simulations is first discussed. Then, the precision synthesis strategies for constructing atomically dispersed, long‐range‐ordered, and interfacial‐confined heteroatomic structures are systematically summarized. Subsequently, mechanistic insights into the promoting effect of heteroatoms, driven by synergistic electronic and geometric modulation, are highlighted, followed by an analysis of future research directions and the key challenges for the industrial implementation of heteroatomic catalysts for COxRR. This review provides an integrated perspective linking active‐site design to catalytic performance, offering guidance for the development of next‐generation heteroatomic electrocatalysts for efficient COxRR toward the sustainable production of high‐value chemicals.
n19d2754b28f4: Low‐dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost‐efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one‐pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.
n00884a8350a3: The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li2S in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single‐component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi‐step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high‐entropy complementary d‐band center model, extending the classical d‐band center theory to multi‐metal systems. The complementary d‐band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi‐metal sites collaboratively construct a “highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption” closed‐loop pathway, with the d‐p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high‐entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li‐S batteries.
n89c1e780f7a0: Near‐infrared (NIR) imagers are essential for applications ranging from material sorting and autonomous driving to biomedical diagnostics, yet their performance is often limited by severe carrier recombination and high dark current. Here, we demonstrate a low‐noise NIR photodiode based on Te‐TeOx nanocrystalline‐in‐matrix films, in which the surrounding oxide matrix provides in situ bulk passivation and enables the modulation of carrier transport to balance carrier loss and extraction. This approach reduces trap density, suppresses recombination, and prolongs carrier lifetime, while controlled oxide incorporation tunes the optical bandgap and interfacial offsets of the heterojunction photodiode, resulting in spectral response spanning the visible and NIR regions with low dark current. The resulting photodiodes exhibit a low dark current of 9.70 nA cm−2 at a bias of −10 mV, a detectivity of 3.85 × 1012 Jones and an ultralow detectable power of 1.35 pW for NIR photodetection. The strategy is compatible with direct monolithic integration with readout integrated circuits, enabling a 256 × 256 focal‐plane imager with excellent pixel uniformity. It further supports high‐quality focal‐plane imaging in both visible and NIR regions, as well as solution identification and imaging through smoke.
nb3c38132fb43: Electrocatalytic small‐molecule conversion addresses the need to couple renewable electricity with sustainable fuel and chemical production, yet challenges remain in resolving the dynamic gas/solid/liquid interfaces that govern catalytic activity, selectivity and stability. A key challenge is to correlate catalyst structures, reaction intermediates and local interfacial environments under comparable operating conditions. Ambient‐pressure x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provides surface‐sensitive and chemically specific information on catalyst chemical states, interfacial species and local electrostatic environments at the same working interface, enabling direct correlations between catalyst evolution and reaction intermediates. We offer a forward‐looking review of APXPS for probing gas/solid/liquid interfaces in small‐molecule electrolysis. We discuss three categories of electrochemical XPS/APXPS configurations: quasi‐in situ XPS, in which electrochemically treated catalysts are transferred under protected conditions for post‐reaction analysis; thin‐electrolyte‐film (dip‐and‐pull) APXPS, which probes a potential‐controlled interface through a nanometer‐scale liquid film; and membrane‐based APXPS, which accesses catalyst–ionomer–electrolyte interfaces. We introduce present‐day challenges in electrochemical APXPS and describe a vision towards more realistic operating conditions, higher time resolution and multimodal measurements integrated with theoretical and data‐driven spectral analysis. These developments provide potential avenues to establish reliable structure–intermediate–environment relationships in the further development of small‐molecule electrocatalysis.
ndbf9353b2160: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are promising for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their application is limited by sluggish polyiodide redox kinetics and severe shuttle effect. Many cathode‐regulation strategies improve iodine chemistry through physical confinement and polar adsorption. However, simultaneously suppressing polyiodide shuttling and enabling rapid iodine conversion remains challenging, particularly under high‐rate where fast interfacial redox kinetics are required. Here, interface‐confined cationic polarization is established by integrating π‐delocalized guanidinium cations (Gdm+) into iodine cathodes, where cation–π interactions with Ketjen Black (KB) sp2 carbon domains confine Gdm+ on the KB surface. The delocalized positive charge of interface‐confined Gdm+ electrostatically enriches polyiodides within the cathode, while its delocalized π‐electron system polarizes the electron cloud of iodine species and promotes interfacial charge transfer, enabling reversible polyiodide conversion without irreversible trapping. The optimized I2 cathode delivers 100 mAh g−1 at an ultrahigh‐rate of 50 A g−1 (∼237 C) and sustains 40 000 cycles with only 0.002% decay per cycle. A 1.0 Ah pouch cell retains 82.6% capacity after 1200 cycles. This work demonstrates interface‐confined cationic polarization as an effective strategy for regulating polyiodide redox chemistry, offering a new route toward high‐rate and long‐life Zn–I2 batteries.
n3d7fe4d4a498: The controlled growth of two‐dimensional (2D) non‐layered transition metal oxides remains a key challenge in low‐dimensional material synthesis. Achieving atomically precise construction of 2D structures requires a fundamental understanding of how external fields and interfacial interactions govern nucleation and growth processes. In this work, amorphous NiOx (a‐NiOx) was deposited onto monolayer MoS2, and its transformation into crystalline 2D NiO nanosheets was directly visualized in situ using environmental transmission electron microscopy. The electron beam induces the decomposition of a‐NiOx into mobile NiOx species, which migrate and nucleate on MoS2, demonstrating the synergistic roles of the electron beam and thermal field in NiO cluster formation and interface‐dominated epitaxial growth. Combined notch‐filtered imaging and theoretical calculations reveal that Ni–O units preferentially attach at the NiO/MoS2 interface to form one‐dimensional growth fronts, while oriented attachment proceeds via nanosheet rotation, interfacial fusion, and defect‐mediated reconstruction, culminating in lattice relaxation into a single‐crystalline structure. High‐throughput selected‐area electron diffraction further uncovers the modulation of external fields on the multi‐path structural evolution of NiOx. This work establishes an in situ strategy to resolve nucleation and growth pathways of 2D heterostructures, enabling active control over the 2D growth of non‐layered metal oxides and advancing deterministic atomic‐level construction.
n232e15b69190: Proton‐triggered degradation at the buried interface severely undermines the operational stability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, this work develops an ionization‐state‐directed sulfonate approach using sodium 2,2'‐disulfanediyldiethanesulfonate (DDANA). The pre‐deprotonated sulfonate terminals grant DDANA strong coordination with lead sites and drive its spontaneous aggregation at the perovskite and self‐assembled monolayer interface, forming robust multisite binding with the perovskite lattice. The enriched sulfonate groups build favorable interfacial dipoles to optimize energy level alignment and facilitate hole transport. The immobilized sulfonate groups act as conjugate‐based sites to competitively capture protons, while the disulfide skeleton enables reversible iodine‐redox to scavenge corrosive iodine species under operational stress. Dissociated sodium (Na+) ions embed into lattice interstices and release residual tensile strain. As a result, DDANA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 27.38% (certified 27.13%). The strategy extends seamlessly to flexible devices and rigid large‐area modules, delivering efficiencies of 25.88% and 23.33%, respectively. Moreover, the DDANA‐modified devices retain 98.9% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking and 97.4% after cycling diurnals. This work establishes sulfonate ionization‐state engineering as a versatile molecular design platform for constructing chemically robust buried interfaces toward efficient, stable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
n816129235eb9: Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (NaxSn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the NaxSn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na2O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF2||NaxSn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||NaxSn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g−1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.
n2460b1a97292: Layer‐by‐layer (LBL) fabrication of organic solar cells (OSCs) decouples donor and acceptor deposition, which, however, induces difficulties in controlling donor crystallization and acceptor interdiffusion. Here, we introduce NPSG, a fully conjugated double‐spiro‐grid polymer, to regulate donor fibrillar pre‐assembly before acceptor deposition. Morphological results reveal that NPSG shifts D18 assembly from loosely associated aggregates toward pronounced fibrillar pre‐assemblies in solution. Molecular dynamics simulations further suggest that the rigid NPSG backbone provides multiple noncovalent interaction sites that favor anisotropic association between D18 chain segments. During film formation, these fibrillar precursors evolve into a coherent and solvent‐resistant donor framework, which moderates L8‐BO interdiffusion and promotes a vertically graded, double fibrillar heterojunction. The resulting morphology facilitates interfacial charge transfer, improves the balance of electron and hole transport, and suppresses nongeminate recombination. Consequently, the optimized D18+NPSG/L8‐BO devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.2%, with a certified value of 20.7%. This strategy also improves device reproducibility, processing tolerance, applicability across different donor/acceptor systems, and operational stability under maximum‐power‐point (MPP) tracking. These findings establish donor‐underlayer pre‐assembly regulation as an effective strategy for efficient and robust sequentially processed OSCs.
n7f8f325c1283: Smart luminescent materials (SLMs) represent an emerging class of intelligent optical systems that can convert external stimuli into adaptive and programmable photonic outputs. By integrating molecular photophysics with dynamic structural regulation, SLMs enable precise modulation of emission intensity, wavelength, polarization, lifetime, and energy conversion pathways with high spatiotemporal controllability. Recent advances in molecular engineering, supramolecular assembly, and hierarchical material design have driven a transition from conventional luminescence switching toward multifunctional systems featuring multilevel, multistimulus, and information‐enriched optical responses. This review provides a comprehensive and mechanism‐oriented overview of recent progress in SLMs across diverse material platforms, including solution‐phase systems, solid‐state materials, dynamic hydrogels, chiral circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) systems, and lanthanide‐doped upconversion nanoparticles. Particular emphasis is placed on how external stimuli regulate excited‐state electronic structures, molecular conformations, supramolecular organizations, and hierarchical architectures to achieve adaptive luminescent behaviors. In addition, emerging strategies for stimuli‐responsive CPL regulation and intelligent photon conversion based on upconversion nanomaterials are highlighted, demonstrating how molecular‐level control can be translated into dynamic optical functionalities. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed toward the rational design of next‐generation smart luminescent materials for applications in information security, wearable electronics, soft robotics, biophotonics, and intelligent photonic devices.
nc147434df56e: Magnetic anisotropy is essential for controlling magnetic responses in soft matter, yet it is conventionally imposed using external magnetic fields. Here, we show that magnetic anisotropy can instead be intrinsically encoded and continuously tuned through hierarchical structural organization, establishing a route by which anisotropic dipolar interactions, rather than conventional shape effects, dominate the magnetic energy landscape. This mechanism is achieved by engineering composite nanofibrils in which magnetite nanoparticles are grown in situ within an aligned aramid–silk matrix, inspired by biomineralization in chiton teeth. The resulting aramid–silk–magnetite fibers combine high strength and modulus with exceptional toughness up to 820 MJ m− 3, while exhibiting tunable magnetic anisotropy spanning axial to radial easy-axis configurations through structural relaxation. Quantitative analysis reveals that collective dipolar coupling dominates magnetic anisotropy by orders of magnitude over demagnetization-field contributions, identifying nanoparticle interaction networks as the primary origin of anisotropy. This built-in anisotropy enables strain-mediated reconfiguration of magnetic properties, giving rise to magnetoelastic coupling that scales with fiber modulus and reflects the available structural mobility for magnetic reorientation. By amplifying structure-defined anisotropy under mechanical loading, we further demonstrate strain-controlled magnetic torque for actuation. These findings establish a structural design principle for programming magnetic anisotropy in mechanically robust magnetoelastic materials.
n0a3d6ce13a72: Two-dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular-weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long-range order. Here, we report a gas–solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi-2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single-crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuOx surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination-assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π-stacking-driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer-scale PPA single-crystalline nanoribbons with left-handed cis-transoidal helical chains and long-range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended-chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper-bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 109 g mol− 1. The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W− 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 101 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade-off between molecular-weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi-2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.
n8ca32254205f: The accumulation of microplastics originating from single‐use personal protective equipment presents a growing environmental concern. Developing biodegradable fibrous alternatives is essential, but integrating robust antimicrobial efficacy with stable electrostatic capture while maintaining degradability remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a surface co‐functionalization strategy addressing these challenges through covalent immobilization of sodium copper chlorophyllin (SCC) and quaternary ammonium compounds (QAC). Beyond simple dual functionalization, this molecular design induces intramolecular charge separation, suppressing electron‐hole recombination in SCC and thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species generation under visible light. Simultaneously, QAC introduce permanent cationic surface charges that enable contact‐mediated microbial inactivation and humidity‐resistant electrostatic particle capture. Demonstrated on biodegradable silk nanofibers as a model substrate, the functionalized fibers exhibit potent antibacterial and antiviral activity under both dark and illuminated conditions, together with high nanoparticle capture efficiency. Importantly, the fibers retain intrinsic biodegradability, undergoing near‐complete degradation under enzymatic conditions and substantial decomposition in soil environments. This work establishes a versatile surface functionalization platform applicable to diverse fibrous substrates, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional microplastic‐generating protective materials.
na5c8c4b66630: Biological ion channels achieve multi-ion discrimination through parallel chemically distinct channel types, each optimized for a single ion species. Replicating this within a single synthetic membrane has remained beyond reach, for conventional membrane resistance blocks the bonding energy difference between different ions. Here we show that an ultrathin polymeric membrane (ca. 8.56 nm) bearing aligned angstrom-scale porphyrin pores, fabricated by interfacial superspreading, reduces internal resistance sufficiently and achieves simultaneous multi-ion discrimination. Under a microvolt-scale applied voltage, the membrane separates six ion species across three valence groups. In particular, the membrane exhibits anomalous selectivity for Li+, with a threshold voltage V t ≈ 400 mV which is 370 mV above the nearest competitor. Applied to lithium extraction from low-quality brines, a two-stage device achieves >98% recovery at 1.1 × 10−4 Wh g−1 (Li), three orders of magnitude below conventional electrodialysis. This membrane architecture offers a broadly applicable design principle for energy-intensive separations in which resolving ions of similar charge and size is the critical challenge.
na6a72fae9ab3: Moiré superlattices formed by twisting periodic systems provide a powerful platform for emergent topological phenomena, but their use for programming real‐space topology in acoustic wave fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a phase‐controlled spoof surface acoustic wave platform for constructing moiré topological textures in the acoustic particle‐velocity field. On a perforated acoustic metasurface, two twisted skyrmion lattices are synthesized and superposed, yielding acoustic skyrmion bags with controllable topological numbers and geometries. The twist angle and rotation center control the scale and configuration of the bags, enabling deterministic reshaping of the composite texture. We further introduce controlled defects to assess the defect tolerance of the moiré skyrmion bags. The skyrmion bags retain their composite topology over a finite range of defect fractions, and comparison with an untwisted single‐layer skyrmion lattice suggests enhanced stability of the enclosed skyrmion cluster relative to the single‐layer reference at higher defect fractions. The same programmable platform also supports transitions from skyrmion lattices to meron lattices and enables twist‐induced meron clusters. These findings establish acoustic moiré superlattices as a reconfigurable platform for engineering robust real‐space topological textures, with potential applications in topology‐guided acoustic manipulation and information encoding.
n4fa45386f128: Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine)2(SiF6)]n, SIFSIX-3-Zn, and its recently reported first-generation derivatives [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(SiF6)] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second-generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(NbOF5)] n , NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M, M = Co, Ni, Cu, Zn. The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x-ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as-synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large-pore (lp) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water-loaded lp phases into narrow-pore (np) guest-free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations (np→lp) for Cu and Zn, and rare examples of induced-fit (lp→np→lp) from guest-free lp to np to water-loaded lp phases for Co and Ni. The NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal-dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.
n2d3b283cea8a: Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi‐topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer (MIP) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na+ transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi‐topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.
nc29dbfd7623e: Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well-known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room-temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh)4(H2PO4)·(CH3OH)0.5] (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 ) that exhibits a three-dimensional pillared-layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P21 space group, and its non-centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field (P–E) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm−2. Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric-type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy-harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5–PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage (𝑉oc) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact-type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.
n01c790c98d5d: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp3) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.
na6eaf5124441: Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)-based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt-based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m2 gPt −1) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.
n7a729d381b09: The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp3)─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp2)─N bond to provide fused amines.
n8d1df99a8d34: The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans‐cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.
n3ccbfea61cbf: Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD3) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D2O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13CH3/13CD3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K2CO3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD3 isotopic architectures.
nb14dc5d7663c: Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g−1 h−1—10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0)—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH4. MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni7.5) delivers a CH4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g−1 h−1—28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0) and MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 conversion.
n813f89113899: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)‐rich TiO2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C2H5OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g−1 h−1 with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C2H5OH at 361.5 µmol g−1 h−1 with 99.4% yield‐based selectivity, which is related to Cu2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high‐performance and low‐cost photocatalyst for CO2‐to‐C2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single‐atom–surface‐group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.
nf8711d26f986: Pre-catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre-catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate-dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca-Ni3S2 as the model pre-catalyst and K2CO3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate-dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni3S2 into NiOOH, enabling surface-confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni3S2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca-Ni3S2-RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm−2, a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH-reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca-Ni3S2-RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m−3 H2 to deliver 4000 A m−2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.
nf60439f5c6d8: Rapid advances in A-DA'D-A fused-ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non-radiative energy loss (ΔE 3) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron-deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT-4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron-deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4-c:3′,4′-g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross-coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT-4F exhibits extended π-conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid-state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed ΔE 3 in PM6:CBT-4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced ΔE 3, PM6:CBT-4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT-4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP-eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT-4F as a high-performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors.
n55cf9bfa3ed3: Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.
n0d88162674b5: In a rhenium‐doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high‐valent Re stabilizes low‐valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. Dynamic Re–Ir–O interactions open a hybrid adsorbate‐evolution/oxide‐path mechanism, delivering a 250 mV overpotential, >1,300 A gIr−1 mass activity, and 600 h durability for low‐iridium PEM water electrolysis. More in the Research Article e1466065, Jung Kyu Kim, Young‐Min Kim, Byung‐Hyun Kim, HyukSu Han, and co‐workers.
n396dfd82ce10: Gaining control over chromophore-functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light-harvesting complexes, and photo-redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand (LA ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone (L1 ) or carbazole (L2 ) π-system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L1 or L2 to LA , however, only for cage Pd2 LA 2 L1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L1 -centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra-assembly excitation back-transfer from LA to L1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited-state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S1 states enable excitation back-transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster-type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy-transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co-ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).
n74e51f75438f: Bismuth-based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that selective electrochemical potential control under alkaline conditions can deterministically direct the reconstruction of layered BiOCl precursors, establishing a direct link between applied bias and catalyst structure.
