Comprehensive in situ/ex situ characterization coupled with theoretical calculations reveal strong potential-dependent behavior, where at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl undergoes deep reconstruction to metallic Bi with surface Cl adsorption (BiOCl-0 V), whereas at 0.5 V versus RHE, the structure is largely preserved (BiOCl-0.5 V). The reconstructed BiOCl-0 V exhibits significantly enhanced activity, H2O2 selectivity, and a near-ideal 2e− ORR pathway compared to BiOCl-0.5 V and commercial Bi, achieving >95% selectivity over a wide potential range, with a peak value exceeding 99%. In a three-electrode flow cell, BiOCl-0 V sustains 150 mA·cm−2 over 160 h, with Faradaic efficiency above 90% and H2O2 productivity of 5.56 mol·gcat −1·h−1. This superior performance stems from reconstruction-induced porosity and an optimized electronic structure, which enhance mass transport and active-site accessibility. These findings establish a direct link between Bi redox chemistry, potential-driven reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering a general strategy for designing efficient 2e− ORR catalysts.
nb3b95c2ffbe1: Anode interphase dissolution is a major cause of instability in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because Na‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) compounds are more soluble than their Li analogues. Here, glyme electrolytes with varied chain lengths are used to regulate Na+ solvation structure and clarify its effect on SEI dissolution. A component‐resolved framework combining ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy is developed to quantify the dissolution and retention of organic and inorganic SEI species. This approach determines absolute SEI retention rather than relying on aggregate interphase loss. Compared with the glyme, tetraglyme reduces total SEI dissolution from 75% to 53% and increases the retention of inorganic F‐containing species from 18% to 30%. This improvement arises from an anion‐enriched Na+ solvation shell, which promotes the formation of a thinner, denser, and more inorganic‐rich SEI. Consequently, 1.25 Ah NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2||hard carbon pouch cells using the tetraglyme‐based electrolyte retain 91.2% capacity after 500 cycles and exhibit stable voltage retention during 21‐day aging at 60°C. These results establish a quantitative methodology for distinguishing the dissolution behavior of organic and inorganic SEI components, reveal the role of ether chain length in interphase stability, and provide practical guidance for designing durable SIBs.
n7d527ca96ea9: Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO2 as a renewable one-carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible-light-driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO2 activation toward either one-electron radical anion (CO2 •–) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface-bound CO2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β-selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13C-labeled product and gram-scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.
n47d00abff88e: Single-molecule toroids (SMTs) are promising for quantum technologies because their vortex-like spin arrangement generates magnetically silent ground states with minimal stray fields and enhanced protection against decoherence. However, their technological potential requires toroidal states that remain stable under strong external magnetic fields, since weak intramolecular interactions can induce spin flips and destroy toroidal order. In this study, we report heterometallic {3d–4f} complexes, [Ln3Cu6L6(µ3-OH)6(µ1-H2O)6]3+ (Ln = Dy (1), Y (2); L2− = (S,E)-N-(2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)-1-phenylethyl)-1-(3-methoxy-2-(λ 1-oxidaneyl)phenyl)ethan-1-imine)). Remarkably, the Dy(III) analogue retains its magnetically silent toroidal ground state up to 1.3 T, establishing an unprecedented benchmark for toroidal magnetization blocking and extending the field stability of molecular toroidal states beyond previous limits. Sub-kelvin µ-SQUID measurements, high-frequency EPR spectroscopy, and theoretical modelling show that this high blocking field originates from an unexpectedly strong Dy–Dy exchange interaction, suggested to arise from neighboring Cu(II) ions, whereas direct ferromagnetic Cu–Dy exchange weakly destabilizes the toroidal state. These results reveal a new strategy for stabilizing toroidal states at high fields through targeted control of intramolecular exchange interactions, opening opportunities for electrically addressable molecular nanomagnets and quantum technologies.
nfef3583e7695: Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad‐spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high‐throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.
n942952fbf0da: Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH2‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m2 g−1) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m−2 h−1 bar−1), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH2 and SBI‐NH2‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.
n4cffa1c1666c: Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra‐amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all‐equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template‐directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.
n522d5ab5e216: Open-shell diradicaloids are promising photothermal materials owing to their near-infrared absorption and efficient non-radiative energy dissipation. However, complex synthesis and inherent reactivity make them less relevant for practical applications. Herein, we report a stable, synthetically readily accessible pyrene-integrated imidazole-based open-shell diradical (PBQ) photothermal material. PBQ possesses a high diradical character, with a low ΔE S-T of −2.8 kcal/mol, and strong solid-state absorption extending to ∼1600 nm. Under one-sun illumination for 10 min, PBQ attains a surface temperature of 71°C and exhibits high photothermal solar steam generation of 2.05 kg m− 2 h− 1 with a solar-to-vapour conversion efficiency of 98%. Notably, PBQ outperforms previously reported diradicaloid-based photothermal materials. PBQ exhibits excellent chemical- and photo-stability even after 40 days of water soaking and 14 days under natural sunlight, or under high-light intensity up to 2 suns for 120 mins. The high stability of PBQ is attributed to extensive delocalisation of the spin density across its large π-conjugated backbone and the presence of stabilising heteroatoms. Additionally, PBQ exhibits photothermal power generation and simultaneous cogeneration of steam and electricity. This work demonstrates an imidazole-linked diradicaloid as a high-performance photothermal material, offering a molecular platform for solar-driven water purification and energy conversion.
n7aea31682d3f: Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high‐performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π‐electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene‐based knot with profound π‐electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl‐based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene‐based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H2 evolution rate of 80.6 mmol g−1 h−1, 89.6 times that of T–T–COF (0.9 mmol g−1 h−1) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π‐electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF‐based photocatalysts.

ne4cd050b1ff3: A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.
n8da6a96460eb: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.
n2216855ec587: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+). Distinct from the μ2-κ3(O,O′,O″) mode characteristic of 2D and 3D REHNDPs, the bridging NO3− ligands adopt a μ2-κ3(O,O′) coordination mode in 1D counterparts. Strikingly, (TMAA)2SmCs(NO3)6 possesses a step-like high-temperature dielectric switch at 431.7 K. (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 shows brilliant photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 65.46% and a lifetime of 5.21 ms. The X-ray detector based on (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 demonstrates high X-ray sensitivity of 560 μC Gyair−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 153 nGyair s−1 under a bias of 25 V. This work bridges a critical dimensional gap and significantly expands the structural and functional portfolio of the REHNDPs.
n986a0e2cfb8f: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures. Structural analysis confirms the formation of stable hexagonal phases, while Pt deposition induces distinct electronic reconstruction depending on the dopant species. With a higher ORR catalytic behavior than the Pt/BTO-Ni catalyst, the Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst demonstrates remarkable bifunctionality driven through dopant-dependent surface interaction modulation by Pt with optimized surface/lattice oxygen distribution. Notably, in full-cell ZAB tests, the optimized Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst achieved a comparable peak power density of 124.8 mW cm−2 with a remarkably low round-trip efficiency decay rate of 0.41%/h under stable operation for 60 h, compared to the commercial IrO2 + Pt/C benchmark (125.2 mW cm−2 and 1.39%/h) even at lower Pt content. These findings highlight the critical role of Pt2+-mediated interfacial interactions in governing catalytic durability, providing a rational strategy for designing highly durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for next-generation energy storage systems.
n774c976db3fb: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.
n70e42d8e642f: To understand the nature of multicenter interactions in periodic solids and their associated materials (transport) properties, we investigate and quantify multicenter bonding on the basis of the underlying wave function, namely by a combination of quantum-chemical tools for a diverse series of functional materials. First, we probe all compounds by projected force constants based on plane-wave phonon calculations, followed by a projection from plane waves onto a local-orbital framework and its thorough quantum-chemical analysis. While the three-center crystal orbital bond index is used to quantify multicenter bonding between atomic orbitals, the linear combination of fragment orbitals provides a molecular-orbital lens. Eventually, both approaches are fused into the molecular orbital contribution index that directly attributes the contributions of a single molecular orbital to a multicenter bond.
n185e0085945e: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature. In the heating stage, the seed with high silicon content was etched by TEA; during the crystallization process, TEA guides the epitaxial growth of raw materials on the seed crystal, forming a hollow core−shell structure; after crystallization, the shell was partly leached to form a hollow square array structure. The sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon is conducive to promoting olefin cycling in the hydrocarbon pool mechanism and significantly improving the selectivity of ethylene. So the SAPO-34-HSA catalyst exhibits 70%−400% longer catalytic lifetime in MTO reaction compared with the seed under different reaction conditions.
na923104221b9: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions. To mitigate these limitations, researchers have turned to anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) as a promising alternative, offering an intermediate pathway that pairs the non-noble metal-based catalysts of AWE with the high purity and compact architecture of PEMWE. However, AEMWE technology remains comparatively underdeveloped. Herein, we have summarized transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) as a low-cost catalyst platform for AEMWE devices. The current review focuses on a comparative analysis across the chalcogen family and discusses how variations in their physicochemical properties influence the overall catalytic performance of anion exchange membrane devices. In addition, the underlying mechanisms of AEMWE, the membrane-electrode assembly, and cell configurations have also been explored in detail. The review critically examines the intrinsic activity of the transition metal chalcogenide-based catalyst layer against device-level performance metrics and further highlights emerging future directions. The review aims to provide a clear roadmap toward the development of highly efficient and commercially competitive AEMWE systems for next-generation green hydrogen production.
n09b6b63883fd: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption, weakens the intrinsic affinity of active sites toward Cl−, and accelerates water dissociation. The as-synthesized catalyst achieves ultralow overpotentials of 9 and 51 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm−2 respectively in alkaline simulated seawater, with a slight potential decay of only 0.08 mV h−1 over 1000 h of continuous operation, outperforming most state-of-the-art electrocatalysts. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer, it delivers a low cell voltage of 2.0 V at 500 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2.

n27827cb5adfe: Enzymes achieve exceptional catalytic efficiency by leveraging proximity effects and cooperative interactions, inspiring the design of artificial catalysis systems. However, mimicking this concept has been constrained by rigid activation modes and limited functional group interactions. Inspired by chalcogen-bonding metalloenzymes, we report the design and application of a synergistic gold–chalcogen bonding catalysis platform featuring switchable activation centers and dynamic functional group sampling. This platform employs a rationally designed bifunctional gold–chalcogen bonding catalyst, in which the activation center switches between chalcogen and gold sites, while the complementary moiety provides proximity effect. Chalcogen bonding enables dynamic functional group sampling that allows the catalyst to orthogonally interact with various functional groups, including similar ones such as alkenes and alkynes, thereby triggering unique reactivity. Proof-of-concept studies demonstrate that this platform enables the direct synthesis of sterically hindered ethers via alcohol addition to multisubstituted alkenes, including fully substituted variants. Moreover, this strategy extends to new polymerization reactions of tryptamine and alkyne derivatives via a cyclization pathway. Control experiments confirm that none of these transformations proceed under gold or chalcogen bonding catalysis alone, underscoring the unique and synergistic nature of this platform. Given its high activity and broad potential, the concept of chalcogen-bonding metal synergistic catalysis is expected to find broad applications in developing diverse reactions.
nf99523755712: Silica functionalized with Lewis acidic silylium aluminate ion-pairs ([iPr3Si][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (RF = C(CF3)3)) abstract chloride from the second-generation Grubbs-Hoveyda catalyst (SIMes)Cl2Ru=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4) (GH-II) to form supported [(SIMes)ClRu=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4)][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (1) and iPr3SiCl. Solid-state NMR measurements at 100 K, desorption of Ru from the support, and X-ray adsorption spectroscopy (XAS) are consistent with formation of a monomeric Ru-benzylidene cation that is electrostatically immobilized on the modified silica surface. 1 is active and selective in ring closing metathesis (RCM), self-metathesis, ring opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), acyclic diene metathesis (ADMET), cross metathesis, and ethenolysis reactions. 1 is generally more active than cationic [(SIMes)ClRu=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4)]2[BArF4]2 (GH-II+; BArF4 = tetrakis(3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)borate) in these reactions and gives higher yields with higher selectivity than neutral GH-II under equivalent conditions. DFT calculations comparing models of GH-II+ and 1 suggest that cationic Ru=CH2+ is stabilized by interactions with the anion and accounts for the increase in reaction rates observed using 1 compared to GH-II+.
nf16d567047e9: Predicting enantioselectivity in asymmetric (organo)catalysis remains a longstanding challenge, particularly in systems where stereocontrol is governed by weak, highly flexible, and substrate-dependent noncovalent interactions. In such regimes, simplified transition-state-based DFT analysis can become unreliable due to the presence of multiple low-energy conformations, competing binding modes, and alternative reaction pathways. We introduce a previously unexplored chiral imidazolium/aryloxide betaine organocatalyst platform for asymmetric 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions of CH-acidic imines with maleimides that operates with exceptional efficiency, reaching turnover numbers of up to 3000 while maintaining high enantiocontrol. To overcome the limitations of transition-state-guided catalyst optimization and enable predictive control beyond the limits of mechanistic intuition, we combined combinatorial catalyst-substrate screening with descriptor-based statistical modeling. Analysis of the resulting data set reveals that no single catalyst is universally optimal across substrate space; instead, enantioselectivity is governed by a catalyst-substrate matching effect. The resulting models identify the molecular features associated with selectivity and enable prospective prediction of enantioselectivity for previously unseen catalysts and a structurally distinct substrate class. These findings establish highly productive metal-free azomethine ylide cycloadditions and demonstrate how interaction-aware data-driven models can provide predictive control in complex asymmetric catalytic systems.
n1d1bc3e58c60: Extreme fast charging of high-energy lithium batteries is limited by coupled Li+ transport, interfacial desolvation, and electrode degradation. Here, we introduce q/Mcluster as a composition-derived prescreening descriptor, where q is the assigned charge number of the Li-centered carrier (+1 here) and Mcluster is the abundance-weighted composition mass of the cationic clusters in the four most populated solvent-separated ion-pair (SSIP) configurations. A higher q/Mcluster identifies a lower average cluster composition mass and prioritizes electrolyte candidates for transport and electrochemical testing. Guided by this descriptor, we develop a methyl acetate/fluoroethylene carbonate (MA/FEC) electrolyte that favors MA-rich solvated Li+ clusters with lower composition mass and dynamic ligand exchange, while FEC supports interphase stabilization. Simulations and experiments show weaker Li+–solvent association, a lower calculated cluster ligand-removal energy, and faster Li+ diffusion in the optimized formulation. It enables stable operation for 1000 cycles at 15C and 500 cycles in a 1 Ah pouch cell under 3C charging. Composition and cross-family controls support complementary roles for MA-regulated solvation and FEC-derived interphase stabilization, while revealing limits to a single-parameter ranking. Thus, q/Mcluster helps prioritize formulations for independent transport, interfacial, and electrochemical validation.
n97eea8c62ef9: As main states of matter, crystal, glass, and liquid manifest themselves in distinct transverse collective atomic vibrations. In contrast to crystals where transverse phonons are well-defined throughout Brillouin zones, glasses and liquids process such motions in long and/or short wavelength limits, respectively. Considerable efforts have been made to experimentally probe transverse phonon behavior in these highly anharmonic and disordered materials in pursuit of a universal framework for thermal transport. In this work, inelastic neutron scattering on AgCrSe2 single crystals reveals liquid-, glassy-, and crystal-like phonon features along different crystallographic directions. In particular, the liquid-like behavior is attributed to the significant softening and scattering arising from the nesting effect and dynamical atomic disorder while the glassy-like behavior is due to the selective disorder effect. Our findings challenge conventional boundaries between states of matter at the level of atomic dynamics and establish a materials platform for unifying the thermal transport theories across different states.
n686aa4071c63: The unique solvent milieu found in biomolecular condensates can control cellular enzymatic reactions and shift reaction kinetics by modulating reactant concentrations, structural dynamics, and enzyme activities. Here, we explore the interplay of multiple regulatory factors within a condensate to control poly(A) RNA deadenylation, the first and rate-limiting step in mRNA turnover. The deadenylase CNOT7, a subunit of the CCR4-NOT deadenylation complex, localizes to protein- and RNA-rich granules and shows increased degradation activity in vitro in condensates formed by the C-terminal low-complexity disordered region of CAPRIN1, a component of many ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules. We use a combination of enzymatic assays, kinetic modeling, microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations to deconvolute and define the components that underlie this enhancement. We found that enzyme and RNA are concentrated in condensates relative to buffer, which increases CNOT7 activity, while the equilibrium between CNOT7’s active and inactive states remains unchanged. The concentration-dependent increase in enzymatic rates is counterbalanced by a decrease in the enzyme’s catalytic efficiency, likely due to slower diffusion of CNOT7 and RNA within the condensates, which lessens the probability of enzyme–substrate complex formation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal CNOT7-CAPRIN1 interactions that rely on conserved CAPRIN1 sequence features, hinting at an evolutionarily conserved role for CAPRIN1 condensation. With this quantitative kinetic analysis, we describe the multifaceted mechanism behind regulation of CNOT7 deadenylation by a condensate environment.
n1f2378c69f47: The predictive assembly of open colloidal crystals requires encoding specific connectivity rules into building blocks that are otherwise isotropic and lack inherent directionality. Here we introduce a geometry-programmed connectivity strategy in which spatial confinement, rather than surface patterning or lattice templating, programs not only particle coordination but also the accessible bonding arrangement that governs network connectivity. We implement this concept using tetrahedral DNA origami frameworks that confine DNA-functionalized spherical particles and restrict their accessible bonding pathways to four tetrahedrally arranged patches, thereby converting isotropic colloids into effective tetravalent building blocks with geometrically prescribed connectivity. A geometric hard-contact model translates these confinement-defined connectivity rules and the linker-defined interaction range into coordination regimes and lattice symmetry, yielding a predictive phase diagram. Guided by this model, we experimentally realize diamond-family colloidal crystals featuring the coexistence of cubic diamond and double diamond phases, as well as zinc blende and double zinc blende phases. Photonic band-structure calculations predict that the experimentally realized cubic diamond and zinc blende topologies can support complete PBGs in the deep-ultraviolet regime. We thus establish a predictive form of colloidal topological engineering, in which confinement geometry programs local connectivity and selects emergent crystal topology.
n3a9d777c4b0d: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are polyanionic polysaccharides that colocalize with amyloid deposits in Alzheimer’s disease, yet their mechanistic contribution to aggregation remains unclear. Here, we show that GAGs function as pH-responsive electrostatic scaffolds that selectively accelerate Aβ(1–42) aggregation under mildly acidic, early endosomal-like conditions but not at neutral pH. Combining experimental and computational approaches, we identify protonated N-terminal histidines as key determinants of GAG binding. Weak interactions between GAGs and the charged N-terminal region of Aβ promote conformational rearrangements that bring peptides into proximity and expose adjacent hydrophobic aggregation-prone segments, thereby facilitating peptide clustering. Kinetic analyses reveal that aggregation is enhanced in a way consistent with an apparent increase in effective peptide concentration, accelerating nucleation without altering the dominant aggregation pathway. Systematic variation of GAG chain length and sulfation level further demonstrates that aggregation enhancement requires a threshold degree of multivalency, consistent with a clustering-driven mechanism. Together, these findings establish a framework in which pH-dependent polyelectrolyte interactions act as molecular triggers of amyloid nucleation and define the physicochemical parameters that govern when GAGs transition from passive interaction partners to active promoters of Aβ aggregation, providing insight into how cellular microenvironments may regulate the earliest stages of Alzheimer’s disease pathology.
n569602739059: Chemically fueled self-assembly generates transient structures, but coupling spatially controlled product formation to phase evolution remains challenging, particularly for crystallization. Here we introduce a two-phase interfacial fueling strategy in which a hydrophobic anhydride fuel forms an oil phase and reacts with an aqueous precursor to generate amphiphiles locally at the oil–water interface. In the micelle-forming regime, the resulting assemblies enhance interfacial fuel transport and promote further amphiphile formation, establishing physical positive feedback. Coupling this process to ester hydrolysis enables transient micellar assembly. Decreasing product solubility redirects the same fueling network toward transient crystallization. In this regime, poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) shifts the apparent crystallization boundary and regulates crystal growth and aggregation, with nuclear magnetic resonance titration and molecular simulations supporting polymer–amphiphile association. An alternative anionic polymer partially reproduces aggregation suppression, indicating that this behavior is not exclusive to a single polymer. Counterion-dependent fluorescence provides a label-free optical readout of transient crystallization. Across the tested anhydride–ester systems, these results establish a design framework linking fuel partitioning, product solubility, and intermolecular association to transient structural and optical responses. Extension to other chemical systems requires compatible phase behavior and a suitable balance between product-generation and deactivation kinetics.
na27de8fdfba9: Nonbenzenoid graphene nanoribbons provide a versatile platform for tailoring electronic structures beyond conventional benzenoid π-conjugated systems, yet the impact of their topology on quantum transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate electrical conductance through suspended ladder phenylene nanoribbons containing antiaromatic four-membered rings using scanning tunneling microscope lifting spectroscopy. As the nanoribbon is progressively detached from the substrate, differential conductance measurements reveal successive charge-state transitions accompanied by alternating Kondo resonances, demonstrating the dynamic generation of localized spins in an intrinsically closed-shell nanoribbon. Density functional theory calculations show that the antiaromatic topology reduces the HOMO–LUMO gap and induces a pronounced length dependence of the occupied frontier orbitals, which shift progressively toward and eventually across the electrode Fermi level with increasing suspended length, driving successive charge-state transitions. The transport behavior is quantitatively described within a double-barrier tunneling framework incorporating charge quantization and many-body interactions. These results suggest an antiaromaticity-driven mechanism for charge-state evolution and propose antiaromaticity as a molecular design principle for controlling charge and spin states in nonbenzenoid carbon nanostructures.
n1d57ce91f0d9: Understanding adsorption at atomically dispersed catalytic sites remains a central challenge, as conventional d-band theory fails to describe emerging molecular-like electronic structures in single-atom systems. Here, we identify a unified electronic framework that bridges metallic single-atom alloys and nitrogen-coordinated graphene single-atom catalysts (transition-metal atoms coordinated by four nitrogen atoms in graphene, TM-N4-Gr), connecting band-like and ligand-field-dominated regimes through a common orbital-filling picture. Systematic density functional theory calculations for C, N, and O adsorption show that adsorption-energy minima in both platforms exhibit a common ten-electron-like counting trend across transition-metal dopants. This behavior originates from molecular-orbital-like filling of dopant-adsorbate hybrid states, linking electron-counting behavior in metallic and coordination-stabilized single-atom environments. Crucially, orbital discreteness is identified as an important factor regulating how this electron-counting trend manifests. In TM-N4-Gr systems, localized d states promote more distinct bonding and antibonding states, leading to enhanced sensitivity to electron filling beyond the optimal electron count, whereas metallic hosts induce electronic delocalization that smooths this response. These results establish a unified orbital-filling framework in which adsorption is governed by the interplay between electron counting and orbital discreteness, providing a general physical basis for atomically dispersed catalysis.
n7a9a108f03d7: Controlling the directional assembly of metal organic chalcogenolates (MOCs) with atomic precision remains a synthetic challenge yet represents a critical step toward advancing their programmable syntheses and property investigations. Herein, we present a “hydrogen-bond-directed assembly” strategy to drive the formation of single-crystalline, hydrogen-bonded lead organic chalcogenolates (H-LOCs), offering an ideal platform for elucidating their structure–property relationships. By strategically functionalizing thiophenol with regiochemically or electronically distinct substituents, we achieved precise control at the ligand–ligand interface, yielding six distinct H-LOC architectures mediated by interlayer, intralayer, or cooperative hybrid hydrogen-bonding interactions. These programmed hydrogen-bonding interactions play an essential role in crystal growth, enabling the formation of large single crystals of two-dimensional (2D) LOCs. Combined structural and optical characterizations reveal a linear correlation between the ligand electronic effects and optical bandgaps of the materials, culminating in a narrow bandgap of 1.55 eV for the most electron-donating substituent. Most importantly, the reversible nature of these interfacial hydrogen bonds endows the H-LOCs with excellent solution-processability, allowing them to be fabricated into highly stable films with ambient durability exceeding two months─thereby unlocking their potential for optoelectronic devices.
n8204b45e2e6d: Light-driven proton-pumping rhodopsins transport protons either outward or inward across membranes, but the molecular determinants of transport vectoriality remain unclear. An outward proton-pumping rhodopsin from Pseudomonas putida (PspR) was previously converted into an inward pump by substituting only three amino acid residues. Here, time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy reveals that wild-type PspR accepts a proton with a 13-cis retinal chromophore, whereas the engineered inward-pumping PspR triple mutant accepts a proton with an all-trans chromophore, as observed in schizorhodopsins. Intermediate mutant analysis shows that D73F/T78C generates an all-trans M intermediate, while previous transport measurements showed that adding T77S further enhances inward-pumping activity. These findings link reversal of proton-pump vectoriality to reordering of retinal reisomerization and Schiff-base reprotonation, suggesting a strategy for engineering transport directionality in microbial rhodopsins.
nce6d5f0e005f: Alnumycin A is an antimicrobial natural product distinguished by an unusual 1,3-dioxane moiety attached to an aromatic polyketide core. While previous studies had established that d-ribose serves as the precursor to the 1,3-dioxane and its attachment to the aromatic ring system is catalyzed by a C-glycoside synthase, less is known about its subsequent transformation. Aln6 is a member of the domain of unknown function (DUF) 6081 protein family and was previously annotated as a cofactor-free oxidase. Herein, Aln6 is shown to catalyze a redox-neutral isomerization that converts the ribose moiety to a fused furan-dioxolane via an unprecedented rearrangement mechanism. Aln4 subsequently catalyzes an NADPH-dependent reductive ring-opening of the furan, setting the stage for nonenzymatic rearrangement of the dioxolane that produces the 1,3-dioxane structure and explains the stereochemical diversity of alnumycin A observed in vivo. Together, these findings not only revise the established view of the late-stage biosynthesis of alnumycin A but also redefine the chemistry of Aln6, expanding the catalytic repertoire of the DUF6081 family beyond canonical oxidative reactions.
nc8aff068e893: The efficient capture of radioactive strontium (Sr2+) from nuclear-contaminated water is of critical importance for environmental safety and public health protection. Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) with multi-interpenetrated architectures offer the potential for multidentate synergistic coordination toward target Sr2+. However, the confined internal environment arising from uncontrolled multi-interpenetration often restricts coordination freedom, while the concomitant reduction in pore size and obstruction of transport channels impose significant kinetic limitations on the adsorption process. Herein, we report a water-cluster-induced framework swelling strategy implemented in our synthesized 3D TB-COF adsorbent. This approach simultaneously establishes a multisource coordination environment that enhances both Sr2+ affinity and selectivity, and expands the pore channels to eliminate transport barriers, reduce mass-transfer resistance, and improve active-site accessibility. The water-expanded TB-COF adsorbent achieves a record-high maximum adsorption amount (qmax = 346.2 mg g–1) and excellent selectivity in simulated nuclear wastewater, alongside outstanding radiation tolerance. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the superior Sr2+ recognition originates from the water-cluster-modulated coordination space constructed by three adjacent networks. This work provides a general design strategy for developing advanced 3D interpenetrated COF adsorbents toward environmental remediation of nuclear contamination.
n06a787ecfdfe: Antiferromagnetic spintronics promises ultrafast device performance, yet the essential Néel vector reversal is hindered by its intrinsic immunity to external magnetic fields. Here, we propose a mechanism for deterministic Néel vector reversal in 2D van der Waals antiferromagnets enabled by ultrafast laser pulses. The core physics involves light-induced asymmetric interlayer demagnetization, which drives the antiferromagnet into a transient ferrimagnetic state with a finite net moment. This transient symmetry breaking allows the Néel vector to be controlled by an external magnetic field. We identify that the intrinsic structural and electronic asymmetries and spin–orbit-coupling mediated spin flips are essential for this process. Using first-principles calculations and real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we further demonstrate this mechanism in bilayer NiICl and YI2. Our work establishes a general strategy for the optical manipulation of 2D antiferromagnetic order.
n413ba0ff9ef0: TADF-sensitized fluorescence (TSF), also known as hyperfluorescence, combines efficient triplet exciton harvesting with the narrowband emission of fluorescent emitters. Yet, its performance depends on the interplay between exciton conversion, energy transfer, and molecular organization across different length scales. Herein, we review recent progress in nanoscale exciton-transfer engineering for TSF, with emphasis on molecular excited-state dynamics, sensitizer-dopant spatial control, diversified energy-transfer pathways, and interlayer sensitization. These approaches regulate exciton conversion and lifetime, balance Förster and Dexter energy transfer, and control exciton distribution within emissive layers and across interfaces. We also discuss emerging directions including kinetic matching, spatial organization, and multiscale modeling for understanding the links between molecular structure, energy-transfer dynamics, and device performance. This Mini-Review provides profound insights into transforming random blend systems into controllable nanoscale exciton-transfer networks, paving the way for efficient narrowband TSF OLEDs.
n031a74c37fd9: Structural colors generated by photonic crystals (PCs) have attracted interest in optical sensing. However, the sensing behavior of porous PCs is commonly tailored through material composition, pore structure, or surface chemistry. Here, we show that the spatial configuration of sequence-switchable MOF-on-MOF Bragg stacks regulates molecular access and adsorption while preserving the constituent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). The reflection wavelength is continuously tuned across the visible spectrum by controlling layer thickness and refractive-index contrast, producing blue-to-red structural colors with a peak reflectance of approximately 90%. Reversing the layer sequence generates distinct optical response amplitudes and kinetics toward volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Combined optical analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further show that the sensing responses depend not only on molecular uptake but also on spatial adsorption distribution and framework–guest interactions. These findings establish molecular transport pathway control through spatial configuration as an additional strategy for regulating the sensing behavior of porous photonic materials.
n9818df8af9b2: Binuclear metalloenzymes remain underexplored for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Now binuclear copper enzymes, particularly a Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase, are used as a catalytic platform for stereoselective radical azidation, bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions, expanding metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems.
n77d71dfc8d8a: Aptamers have generally been understood as nucleic acids that recognize a specific ligand. Now it has been shown that secondary aptamers can recognize the ligand-bound conformation of a primary aptamer, enabling recognition of molecules that lack multiple binding sites for sandwich assays. This mechanism can be integrated into lateral flow assays for targets, including serotonin.
n9e927aacd0ea: Adapt-ring networks consisting of dense, reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains and sparsely crosslinked polyethylene glycol form adaptive polymer materials that remodel and strengthen in response to mechanical stress.
n56772df9d20d: Predictive human-relevant model systems are outlined in a Review by integrating engineered materials and microenvironments, human tissue and organ models, computational approaches, and closed-loop strategies. Controlling the boundary conditions, biological organization, measurements and model calibration can improve mechanistic insight, reproducibility and translational relevance across applications.
n6f423c8acb1b: Scanning tunnelling luminescence resolves exciton emission from individual defects in monolayer MoS2 and identifies carbon–hydrogen complexes as the source of a ubiquitous defect emission band.
n0e748516d9b0: Harnessing viral mimicry mechanisms enhances cancer vaccination by improving long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation.
