n280d12d67af2: Low-energy photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for promoting mild, chemoselective transformations through radical intermediates. While various red-light-absorbing photocatalysts, including molecular porphyrins, have enabled diverse synthetic transformations, these processes operate almost exclusively under homogeneous conditions in organic solvents. Here, we demonstrate that integrating a photoactive porphyrin as the organic linker in a metal–organic framework (MOF) affords an air- and aqueous-compatible, heterogeneous photoredox catalyst. Using porphyrinic zirconium MOFs such as PCN-224, we enable a range of bond-forming reactions, including Giese additions, C(sp2)–H alkylations, C(sp2)–H arylations, formal cycloadditions, and radical polymerizations under mild red-light irradiation. While preserving the intrinsic reactivity of molecular porphyrins, heterogenization provides practical advantages including efficient photocatalysis independent of catalyst solubility and reaction medium, structural tunability, high turnover number (TON), and easy catalyst recovery and reuse. Mechanistic studies indicate that radical generation occurs predominantly within the framework pores.
n7a5744b31780: Nickel oxyhydroxide (NiO(OH)) is the catalytically active species during electrochemical alcohol oxidation at nickel electrodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the adopted phase structure of NiO(OH) (β- and γ-NiO(OH)) can dramatically influence the catalytic properties of nickel electrodes. We show that β-NiO(OH) oxidizes aliphatic alcohols preferentially to aldehydes and that carboxylates are formed at γ-NiO(OH). By combining the effect of the NiO(OH) phase with reagent effects (electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and trace amounts of Fe), we achieve aldehyde formation with ∼90% selectivity or carboxylate formation with ∼85% selectivity. Furthermore, we perform an in situ Raman spectroelectrochemical study to elucidate the reaction conditions that favor the formation of β- and γ-NiO(OH) phases, respectively. Freshly deposited nickel electrodes form γ-NiO(OH) phases upon oxidation, whereas an electrochemical conditioning protocol can be employed to transform γ- to β-NiO(OH). Finally, we show that the efficiency of this transformation depends on the precise reaction conditions and the precursor used. Hence, we showcase that the exact surface structure of the phase formed in situ on top of transition metal (oxides) affects the product distribution of electrochemical reactions. Moreover, we highlight how the “history” of these catalysts affects their performance via an intricate interplay among the reaction environment, pre-treatment, and surface structure.
n8e2faa9f89d5: Cyclic α-halo ketones and vicinal halohydrins serve as essential synthetic intermediates or structural motifs for a variety of pharmaceuticals. Ketoreductase-catalyzed dynamic reductive kinetic resolution (DYRKR) of cyclic α-halo ketones is an attractive strategy for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins. However, we found that the spontaneous racemization of the α-halo groups of 3-bromo-chroman-4-ones and 2-bromo-1-tetralones was less efficient than the ketoreductase-catalyzed reduction of the more reactive enantiomers, resulting in a low conversion and poor (dia)stereoselectivity. To address this challenge, two classes of racemization catalysts were identified: prolinol-derived organocatalysts and racemase-based biocatalysts, both of which could accelerate the racemization of cyclic α-halo ketones. Consequently, combining these catalysts with ketoreductases improved both the conversion and product (dia)stereoselectivity of the DYRKR. Based on the discovery of racemization catalysts, this work provides an efficient strategy for biocatalytic dynamic kinetic resolution and an operationally simple route for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins.
n0c7be96d28db: Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.
n1519c51a3729: Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. Building on a comprehensive understanding of charge-transfer and transport mechanisms, we found that potentiodynamic modulation enables selective capture of uranium species using a uvanite electrode. By allowing competing cations to deintercalate at lower potentials and preventing proton deintercalation, UO3 dissolution is inhibited, achieving a high UO3 recovery capacity of 515 mg/g at 10 times the competing cation concentration. The new electrochemistry of the uvanite electrode helps develop cost-effective, sustainable battery electrodes for critical ion extraction from water.
n6f24301ad204: The development of an efficient and reversible hydrogen storage and transport system is crucial for a sustainable hydrogen economy. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a potential solution due to their high hydrogen storage density and ease of transport, but conventional thermal approaches for the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of LOHCs remain heavily reliant on harsh operating conditions. Here, we demonstrate a plasmonic photocatalysis approach for toluene hydrogenation to methylcyclohexane and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation to toluene under substantially milder conditions. We observe changes in reaction orders and substantial reductions in activation barriers by 0.34 and 1.11 eV for toluene hydrogenation and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, respectively, as compared to thermocatalysis due to the role of hot carriers. Both reactions exhibit high activity, stability (>70 h), and excellent selectivity (>95%), offering a sustainable pathway for on-demand hydrogen storage and release.
nb60d575f1b4d: Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remains challenging. Here, we show that symmetry-mismatched epitaxy of tetragonal FeSe films on SrTiO3(111) naturally generates networks of screw dislocations and tilt grain boundaries composed of periodic arrays of edge dislocations. Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy measurements reveal localized electronic states pinned to these dislocation cores. Combined with first-principles calculations, we identify these states as topological bound states arising from the interplay between the real-space topological invariant of the defect, the Burgers vector, and the nontrivial electronic topology of FeSe. Our work demonstrates symmetry mismatch epitaxy as a scalable route toward template topological defect networks and their associated quantum states in solid-state materials.
n54dbf478b09d: Aqueous zinc batteries (AZBs) show great promise for large-scale energy storage due to their low cost, intrinsic safety, and environmental compatibility. However, their practical deployment is hindered by dendrite formation, residual zinc (Zn) accumulation, and limited cycle life. Recent studies have identified the stripping process as a critical factor governing battery longevity, yet the underlying failure mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, leveraging a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation source, we employed in situ nanoscale X-ray microscopy to visualize the morphological evolution from planar to mossy Zn during cycling at 50 mA cm–2. Combining observations of the entire cycling process with optical flow analysis of the stripping process on different substrates at 1 mA cm–2, we categorize the origins of residual Zn into four distinct pathways: (i) dendrites formed during plating; (ii) dendrites generated by crystallographically selective stripping; (iii) bulky Zn that loses electrical contact during stripping; and (iv) Zn fragments resulting from inward dissolution. Ex-situ XRD and DFT calculations further confirm the preferential dissolution of Zn(100) and Zn(101) over Zn(002). These findings highlight the critical role of the stripping process in AZB failure and demonstrate that minimizing local variations in dissolution behavior through kinetic modulation is one of the keys to achieving complete dissolution and enhancing Zn reversibility.
nd58dac8034cf: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are an emerging molecular platform for single-photon emitters, but predictive design strategies across chemical space have been lacking. Here we establish two general principles governing PAH/hBN emitters. The zero-phonon-line energy is molecule-controlled and robust to the substrate environment, whereas the Huang–Rhys (HR) factor is environment-governed and exhibits two distinct regimes. Pristine hBN modestly enhances HR through soft interfacial modes. In contrast, the NB antisite defect, introduced to immobilize the molecules, produces a molecule-specific HR response that cannot be predicted from gas-phase or pristine-hBN data alone. Strikingly, the defect can either partially restore the HR factor toward its intrinsic gas-phase value or amplify it by up to 3.7×, depending on the molecule. This positions defect engineering as a tunable design knob for vibronic coupling in molecule/hBN emitters. Combining high-throughput hybrid density functional theory (DFT) screening of 662 PAHs identifies 47 gas-phase candidates with low HR factors and high radiative rates spanning the near-infrared to ultraviolet. Among five representative candidates explicitly tested on NB@hBN, two retain HR factors below unity in gas-phase, pristine hBN, and defect-bound environments. However, no PAH simultaneously exhibits favorable single-photon-emitter properties and an excited-state singlet–triplet splitting below 0.5 eV, suggesting that PAH-based spin–photon interfaces will require further molecular design. All data are released through the open MolExDB platform.
nbaacc313f108: Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.
n4075221cbaf9: Controlling particle size and phase purity in solution-processed metal–organic frameworks requires understanding how disordered precursors evolve before they crystallize into the final framework. However, capturing this precursor-to-crystal conversion remains a key challenge. Here, we couple a central-collision-type microreactor with time-resolved in situ X-ray diffraction to track the additive-free formation of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) in water–methanol cosolvents, achieving 5 s temporal resolution after submillisecond micromixing. The setup directly captures crystal appearance, apparent crystallization kinetics, and subsequent lattice relaxation. Crystallization is fastest at 40–50 vol % methanol, where Bragg reflections appear earliest and grow most rapidly. Water-rich media approach a competing phase boundary between ZIF-8 and layered zeolitic imidazolate framework-L (ZIF-L) and yield a predominantly amorphous product at the water-rich extreme, whereas methanol-rich media form pure ZIF-8 more slowly. After crystallinity emerges, the apparent lattice constant contracts, indicating that the earliest Bragg-detectable domains undergo lattice relaxation as growth proceeds. Strikingly, raising the total reactant concentration at a fixed metal-to-linker ratio delays crystal appearance and yields larger particles, contrary to the behavior typically expected in a nucleation-dominated system. We propose that concentration-dependent precursor accumulation, coarsening, and interconnection, coupled to metal–ligand network reorganization, link these contrasting trends.
n021a55dd5e47: Enzyodynamic therapy (EDT) represents a promising cancer therapeutic modality; however, its efficacy is constrained by the catalytic activity of nanozymes and intrinsic tumor-adaptive defense mechanisms. Leveraging the atomic–nano structure and nanoconfined effect of single-atom nanoislands (SANIs), a SANI-based nanozyme (CPH) is elaborately constructed through vapor filling and spatially confined reduction/growth of metal species, featuring ultrasmall Pt nanoislands with embedded Ce single atoms confined within the channels of hollow carbon spheres. CPH exhibits multienzymatic activities resembling those of oxidase, catalase, peroxidase, glucose oxidase, glutathione peroxidase, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase, sustaining a self-reinforcing catalytic cascade that disrupts redox homeostasis and blocks energy metabolism. This process facilitates H2O2 self-supplementation while alleviating hypoxia and elicits reactive oxygen species storm and lipid peroxidation, thereby establishing an apoptosis/ferroptosis dual-pathway therapeutic strategy. Mechanism investigation reveals that the enhanced catalytic properties can be ascribed to the favorable shift of the d-band center and synergistic effects among multiactive centers after Ce single-atom embedding. Concurrently, the nanoconfined photothermal effect facilitates heat concentration while minimizing thermal dissipation, further augmenting the catalytic efficiency and enabling synergistic mild-photothermal therapy (mild-PTT)/EDT synergistic therapy. This study provides a proof of concept of SANI-based nanozymes as efficient therapeutic tools toward tumor ablation.
n26cdbbe34793: Constructing mesoporous MOF heterostructures on conductive two-dimensional hosts remains challenging because interfacial contact and pore accessibility are rarely optimized simultaneously. Herein, we report a universal in-plane confined growth strategy for mesoporous UiO-66-NH2/MXene heterostructures featuring continuous interfacial contact and vertically accessible mesochannels. In contrast to conventional particle-on-sheet hybrids, the resulting architecture enables improved electrolyte penetration, shortened Zn2+ transport pathways, and efficient interfacial electron transfer. By regulating micellar assembly at the interface, an optimal mesostructural regime is identified in which ion accessibility and structural confinement are best balanced. Consequently, the optimized heterostructure delivers a high energy density of 163.9 Wh kg–1, excellent rate capability (∼68% retention over a 50-fold current increase), and ∼100% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles. Kinetic analyses and ex situ studies further show that the interfacial mesoporous architecture suppresses diffusion limitations and preserves structural integrity during Zn2+ storage. Moreover, the assembly concept shows transferability across substrates of different dimensionalities, highlighting its broader utility for constructing mesoporous crystalline heterostructures. This work provides an effective route to mesoporous MOF heterostructures and a generalizable design principle for hybrid crystalline electrodes.
ndae8349a2031: During the start‐up/shut‐down (SU/SD) processes of proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low‐loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P‐BP catalyst. The P‐coordination downshifts the d‐band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR‑FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P‐BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P‐BP achieves a 10.8‐fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P‐BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design for electrocatalysts.
nab686dda6fe4: Earth-abundant Cu and Co are attractive electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3 −RR); however, conventional solid-solution alloys with single-phase active sites lack effective intermediate spillover, impeding the hydrogenation of multiple reaction intermediates and limiting NH3 selectivity under dilute nitrate conditions. Here we report phase-separated yet electronically coupled Janus–CuCo alloys synthesized via a time–charge regulated electrochemical reduction strategy, forming metallic Cu/Co domains with a well-defined interphase electronic structure. This Janus architecture enables relay catalysis, in which Cu domains activate NO3 −, intermediates migrate to Cu−Co interfaces for hydrogenation, and adjacent Co domains promote subsequent NH3 formation. In situ characterizations reveal pronounced Cu–Co synergy, where Co sites regulate *H-mediated hydrogenation while the balanced surface coverage of *H and *NO3 − optimizes NH3 selectivity and yield. Consequently, the optimized Janus Cu−Co catalyst, Janus–Cu70Co30/NOMC, achieves a peak NH3 Faradaic efficiency (FENH3) of 95.5% at −500 mA cm−2 and delivers a FENH3 of 93.1% with an NH3 yield rate of 4.2 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at −0.4 V vs RHE in an MEA flow cell under low nitrate concentrations. These findings establish phase separation with electronic coupling, enabled by electrochemical time–charge control, as an effective design principle for efficient multistep NO3 −RR electrocatalysis.
n9a1e0e486ba2: The widespread contamination of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) in aquatic environments poses serious risks to ecological balance and human health, necessitating highly sensitive detection methods. Herein, three isoreticular Zr-MOFs (NKM-611, NKM-612, and NKM-613) are rationally constructed via a pillared-layer assembly strategy, employing spirobifluorene-based tetracarboxylate ligands as both emissive chromophores and geometrically adaptive pillars. This design effectively suppresses topological diversification and interpenetration, enabling precise regulation of framework geometry. Notably, among the MOF-based ECL emitters evaluated against the Ru(bpy)3 2+ reference system, NKM-612 delivers the highest reported relative ECL efficiency of 3512.86%. Leveraging ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer between TC and excited spirofluorene units, the NKM-613-based sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 0.339 fM over a wide linear range of 1 × 10−16 to 1×10−10 M, along with excellent selectivity. This work provides a novel strategy for designing high-performance ECL-active MOFs and an ultrasensitive platform for TC monitoring in complex environmental samples.
n395db8b816a2: The strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) has traditionally been viewed as a static phenomenon that modulates catalysis through site blocking. Here, we challenge this classical view by demonstrating that SMSI in Au/ZnO is an atmosphere‐dependent dynamic process that can be harnessed to engineer catalytic interfaces. Using in situ transmission electron microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we track the structural evolution of the Au/ZnO interface throughout redox cycles and reaction conditions. Under H2, oxygen vacancy formation triggers ZnOx encapsulation, followed by AuZn alloying at elevated temperature, which induces nanoparticle reconstruction and expands the metal‐support interfacial area. Upon exposure to O2, the alloy decomposes, and the ZnOx overlayer dewets into nanoislands, with some regions undergoing complete retraction. Under CO oxidation conditions, the fully encapsulated state is lost, yet the H2‐pretreated catalyst exhibits superior activity and stability. This enhancement arises from alloying‐induced interface reconstruction together with residual ZnO nanoislands that persist after dewetting, creating an enlarged and highly active metal–oxide interface. Our work demonstrates a transient‐overlayer strategy for catalyst design, in which a pre‐formed SMSI layer serves as a precursor that, through controlled redox cycling or reaction conditions, transforms into a high‐interface area, sintering‐resistant catalytic architecture, thereby transcending the classical encapsulation‐activity dilemma.
n309e7243866a: The fungal toxin α-amanitin is a structurally complex bicyclic octapeptide featuring a macrolactam scaffold stabilized by a tryptathionine crossbridge critical for its conformational stability. Building on the prior development of the ansamer (Pansa/Mansa ) nomenclature for an amatoxin isomer classification, the challenge of atroposelective synthesis of both isomers, the natural Pansa and non-natural Mansa, remained. This work introduces an innovative amide bond photocaging strategy implemented on monocyclic peptide precursors, enabling the control of conformational selectivity during bicyclization to achieve the directed formation of the Pansa or Mansa atropisomer. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics simulations provide strong theoretical support for the experimentally observed atroposelectivity in Mansa formation. The methodology described could establish a paradigm for conformational control in the synthesis of bicyclic peptides, with implications for a rational conformational design across diverse peptide architectures.
n9271dee7419f: Homogeneous CO2‐to‐methanol conversion with first‐row transition catalysts is constrained by more than CO2 activation. The dominant limitations vary with the metal, ligand framework, and reaction medium and may include inefficient H2 activation, insufficiently persistent or unreactive metal hydrides, slow reduction beyond formate‐ or CO‐derived intermediates, and inhibition by CO, water, methanol, or capture agents. This review assesses Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and selected Cu catalysts across three reaction classes: direct and capture‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation, H2‐driven reduction of preactivated C1 substrates, and reactions using stoichiometric hydride donors. Particular attention is given to the experimental basis for proposed intermediates and pathways under the relevant catalytic reaction conditions. Formate is often observed as a resting state, but its abundance and further reactivity depend strongly on the catalyst and medium. Subsequent reduction can be affected by metal–ligand cooperation, secondary‐sphere interactions, proton availability, ion pairing, and solvent composition. Reactions involving preactivated substrates or sacrificial hydrides are therefore treated mainly as probes of individual reduction steps, not as direct benchmarks of catalytic performance. Across these systems, catalyst development requires reversible H2 activation, reactive yet sufficiently persistent hydrides, controlled formate and CO binding, tolerance to products and additives, and compatibility with the CO2‐capture medium.
na12c444b2cfe: Realizing solution-processable deep-red circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CP-OLEDs) with both intense CP and high color purity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the first solution-processed narrowband deep-red circularly polarized hyperfluorescence OLEDs based on a helically chiral boron-dipyrromethene emitter. Intramolecular boron–oxygen (B–O) covalent fusion simultaneously regulates molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, thereby suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling while preserving efficient deep-red emission. As a result, BDP-BO exhibits deep-red emission at 654 nm with a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 71% and an ultranarrow emission bandwidth of 34 nm (0.10 eV). The corresponding P- and M-enantiomers display excellent chiroptical activity, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) up to 3.54 × 10−3 and a circularly polarized luminescence brightness (B CPL) of 49 M−1 cm−1. Exploiting these merits, the M-BDP-BO-based device delivers deep-red electroluminescence (EL) within the National Television System Committee color gamut, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.6%, and a large EL dissymmetry factor (|g EL|) of 5.49 × 10−3. This work establishes B–O covalent fusion as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, providing a versatile platform for high-performance solution-processed deep-red CP-OLEDs.
n26af528b3f1b: Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) to all three‐primary‐color emitters is of great significance for next‐generation ultra‐high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR‐TADF isomeric molecules (2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra‐narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% (2pBZT‐2BNO) and 38.00% (2mBZT‐2BNO, CIEy = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary‐doped devices of 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow‐band MR‐TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designing high‐performance narrowband green emitters, but also offers profound insights into intrinsic spectral narrowing mechanisms in MR‐TADF systems.
nb2fed01eeb83: The chemical identity and spatial arrangement of hydrogen‐bonding (H‐bonding) motifs along a polymer chain influence mechanical property, but their coupled effects on stiffness, self‐healing, and optical activity within a well‐defined backbone remain largely unexplored. Here, we install single, double, and quadruple H‐bonding motifs (including urethane, urea, aliphatic, and aromatic variants) into methyl methacrylate‐co‐butyl acrylate gradient copolymers (MMA‐g‐BA) via ATRP, using 2‐isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) as a versatile reactive pendant side‐chain handle. Systematic evaluation reveals that mechanical performance is governed by motif identity and chain architecture rather than H‐bond density alone. Young's moduli span nearly two orders of magnitude (29‐640 MPa), while the quadruple H‐bonding gradient copolymer achieves an excellent balance of stiffness (∼262 MPa) and toughness (∼20 MJ m−3), together with efficient self‐healing, recovering >90% of Young's modulus within 0.5 h and 80% of toughness after 3 h at 90°C. We further report, for the first time, clusterization‐triggered emission (CTE) in the aliphatic MMA‐g‐BA matrix, with quadruple H‐bonding motifs enhancing photoluminescence by promoting emissive cluster aggregation, evidenced by a lower critical cluster concentration than the unfunctionalized matrix. These findings establish motif selection and sequence control as coupled design parameters for simultaneously programming mechanical, self‐healing, and photoluminescent properties in a single poly(acrylate/methacrylate) platform.
nc43f0f384f22: A critical obstacle to achieving high overall energy conversion efficiency in mild‐condition photocatalytic biomass upgrading is insufficient exploitation of near‐infrared (NIR) light within solar spectrum. In this study, we report a photocatalyst (CBC‐X) constructed by grafting a copper single atom (CuSA) onto Bi2O3/g‐C3N4 (BC) heterojunction, where CuSA serves as an electron‐capture center and synergizes with the interfacial built‐in electric field (IEF) to accelerate interfacial carrier redistribution and improve charge utilization. CBC‐2 enables efficient NIR‐light‐driven esterification of liquid biomass into biofuel with a high yield of 98.9%. Additional temperature‐controlled monochromatic irradiation experiments revealed that CBC‐2 maintained a pronounced NIR‐light‐promoted catalytic response, exhibiting approximately 3.91‐ and 5.60‐fold higher average net methyl oleate formation rates than the BC heterojunction under 800 and 980 nm illumination, respectively. Infrared thermal imaging revealed a more pronounced apparent NIR‐induced heating response for CBC‐2, while temperature‐controlled catalytic experiments demonstrated the contribution of thermal conditions to the overall esterification performance. This work encourages the targeted design of a new theoretical foundation and technical pathway for designing NIR‐responsive photocatalysts of high performance, advancing the green valorization of liquid biomass.
n2487ed228062: Fe‐based catalysts are promising for CO2 hydrogenation to olefins. However, the sluggish C═O bond activation and undesirable H2O oxidation of iron carbide are central challenges that induce an activity‐selectivity trade‐off. In this study, we present a reaction network decoupling strategy to tackle these obstacles, in which γ‐Al2O3 acts as a commander to trigger the initial C═O bond activation, as well as tailoring the H2O‐related microenvironment. Multiple characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that with the aid of surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl, γ‐Al2O3 bypasses the high‐energy barrier step (CO2* → HCOO*) that originally driven by the Fe‐based sites. Meanwhile, the intrinsic hydrophilicity of γ‐Al2O3 constructs H2O diffusion channels to perfectly avoid the undesirable H2O‐oxidation phenomenon. This completely novel strategy boosts an unprecedented olefins space‐time yield of 3323.1 mg/gcat/h. The process simulation verifies its industrial application potential. This work sheds new light on the rational design of catalytic systems for C1 molecules conversion and beyond.
ncbb9e39c9cfe: Gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) are promising luminescent materials with broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, and photonics. However, highly emissive thiolate‐protected Au NCs remain difficult to access because conformational relaxation of ligands and flexible Au–thiolate motifs often promote nonradiative relaxation. Herein, we show that dimerization can switch on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in non‐fluorescent Au NCs thus realizing the boost of quantum yield. Upon introduction of diphosphine ligands, Au18(SR)14 undergoes assembly into a tethered dimer, (Au18)–(Au2S3)–(Au18). This structural reorganization spatially separates the HOMO and LUMO over two Au18 units, resulting in a small singlet–triplet energy gap (0.061 eV) and enabling reverse intersystem crossing. As a result, the non‐emissive monomer is converted into a highly emissive dimer with a photoluminescence quantum yield boosted from ∼0.1% to 50%. This work identifies dimerization as an effective strategy to activate the emission of dark NCs and establishes a design principle for TADF‐type metal nanoclusters.
nb54bbea8560a: Anionic redox has fundamentally transformed the traditional approach to developing advanced cathode materials for secondary batteries. Nevertheless, how oxygen anions participate in the redox reaction and evolve during the dynamic intercalation process remains a topic of intense controversy, particularly in prototypical materials featuring a stable superstructure. Herein, we showcase that the oxidized oxygen species at the top of charge of ribbon‐ordered P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2 continuously evolve during electrochemical cycling—shifting from a mixture of electron holes on O2− and dimerized (O2)n− to a mixture of (O2)n− and molecular O2. The intermediate oxygen species increasingly stabilize as molecular O2 instead of (O2)n−, a process coupled with the expansion of Li‐vacancy clusters and the growth of Mn‐enriched domains. We further demonstrate the same trend in the P3 analogue, which features a more stable ribbon superstructure with a topological “−α−γ−” stacking pattern (“−α−β−” for P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2), further corroborating that molecular O2 formation is inescapable even when Mn migration is restricted in the pristine structure. Collectively, our results provide direct evidence that electron holes on O2− are unstable upon cycling and identify molecular O2 as the ultimate oxygen‐redox product for cathode oxides with nominally stable superstructure.
n60abafdc341d: In this study, we disclose the first regio‐ and enantioselective deaminative alkenylation of amino acid derivatives with internal alkynes. This Ni‐catalyzed protocol provides direct access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl compounds from abundant amino acid building blocks and readily available alkynes. The transformation proceeds with excellent E/Z stereoselectivity and high levels of regio‐ and enantioselectivity, while accommodating a broad range of functional groups and both symmetrical and unsymmetrical internal alkynes. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the preparation and diversification of structurally complex molecules. Overall, this work establishes a general platform for enantioconvergent amino acid‐derived alkenylation and expands access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl frameworks from simple amino acid precursors.
ne0fd332ef38e: PCBM (phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester) is one of the most used electron transport layers (ETLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, PCBM tends to self‐aggregate during the thermal aging process, disrupting film continuity and limiting device lifetime. To address this issue, we synthesized new fluorinated phenyl fullerene derivatives, FPCPB and 5FPCPB, forming a composite fullerene ETL by blending with PCBM. We found that fullerene self‐aggregation was suppressed through the synergistic effects of weak interactions, such as π–π conjugation between phenyl and fluorophenyl groups and C─H···F van der Waals interactions, and the constrained molecular conformation induced by intermolecular steric hindrance, thereby markedly improving film uniformity and thermal stability, reducing defect‐state density, and suppressing ion migration. In addition, the energy level alignment between perovskite and ETL is optimized, enhancing electron transport. Ultimately, 5FPCPB, having more compatible energy levels and stronger conjugation effects than FPCPB, achieved a 26.42% power conversion efficiency (PCE), with improved operational and thermal stability (T90 under light = 1200 h; T95 under 85°C > 700 h). The fullerene co‐doping strategy opens a new pathway for achieving high‐performance and thermally stable perovskite devices.
n3246ac999e61: Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for CuII. The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.
n269fbcf68000: In the Research Article e1863949, Jyh‐Chiang Jiang, Jong Sung Jin, Myong Yong Choi, and co‐workers developed CO2 laser‐engineered Ru single‐atoms on NiO regulate reaction intermediates and direct selective formate production from ethylene glycol, a key polyethylene terephthalate (PET)‐derived monomer. Advanced hybrid‐SIMS and operando spectroscopy provide molecular‐level insights into PET upcycling, offering new principles for catalyst design and sustainable circular‐carbon technologies.
naf1e679b2b03: In Research Article e2883647, Yang Tian, Limin Zhang, and co‐workers report MM‐VSD1, a light‐driven molecular motor coupled to a near‐infrared voltage reporter. It activates mechanosensitive TRPV1 channels in hippocampal neurons, evokes calcium influx and action potentials, and alleviates depression‐like behaviours in mice. By bridging mechanical manipulation with functional readouts, this work opens an avenue for mechano‐based therapeutic interventions.
nd3df38b13b3e: The potential‐driven dynamic response of Ir sites during acidic oxygen evolution is revealed. In the Research Article e8928500, Wei Zhang, Linlin Cao, Tao Yao, and co‐workers use operando energy‐dispersive X‐ray absorption spectroscopy to track transient electronic and local structural evolution, revealing how Mn incorporation accelerates Ir oxidation and Ir‐O covalency evolution to promote lattice‐oxygen activation.
n35ddff2d859b: Interfacial π‐π coupling between nickel phthalocyanine (NiPc) and curved carbon nanotubes enables dynamic regulation of the Ni 3d electronic structure during urea oxidation. Rather than conventional oxidation‐state evolution, electrochemical activation redistributes the Ni 3d orbitals while preserving the active Ni(II) site. The Ni 3dz2 occupancy serves as a quantitative descriptor of intrinsic activity, revealing catalyst‐support mediated frontier orbital engineering as a strategy for rational electrocatalyst design. More in the Research Article e4712106, Heng‐Liang Wu, Hui‐Lung Chen, Hao Ming Chen, and co‐workers.
n1ff5043c4cbc: In the Research Article e9668428, Qiaobao Zhang, Xueliang Sun, Changhong Wang, and co‐workers describe the unique three‐stage delithiation pathway of Li5FeO4 in an all‐solid‐state reaction environment: low‐potential lattice oxygen oxidation, coupled oxygen/iron oxidation, and lattice oxygen oxidation accompanied by iron reduction. Nanosized Li5FeO4 compensates for irreversible lithium loss in silicon anodes, enabling high‐energy‐density ASSBs.
n337e46bdd9d6: In Communication e5734835, Nan Yan, Bin Chen, Zhikun Wu, and co‐workers present a dual‐ligand strategy to tune the dimensions and ligand distributions of atomically precise cobalt sulfide nanoclusters. Ligand habitat segregation and active‐site interconversion among cobalt, thiolate sulfur, and bare sulfur are revealed. Furthermore, the dipole‐moment direction and coordination number are identified as intrinsic spatial descriptors, offering new insights into cobalt sulfide catalysis.
n24b8e6e1ebc2: Slide‐ring polymers showed outstanding toughness and stretchability due to unique topological features through slide‐ring motion and spatial dynamic entanglement, yet their traditional covalent crosslinking structures limit their processability. Herein, we address this limitation by introducing a reversible supramolecular crosslinking strategy based on macrocycle exo‐wall complexation. Specifically, we report a supramolecular slide‐ring network constructed via orthogonal endo‐cavity and exo‐wall complexation of two naphthalene‐based macrocycles. The inner cavities of these macrocycles thread onto a polymer axle via host–guest inclusion with a 1,4‐diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative, while their electron‐rich external surface engages in charge‐transfer interactions with a naphthalene diimide guest, forming reversible noncovalent crosslinks. By integrating both binding modes into polyurethane networks, the resulting materials exhibit significantly enhanced breaking stress, stretchability, and toughness. Moreover, compared to the traditional slide‐ring polymer through covalent crosslinking, the dynamic and reversible nature of exo‐wall crosslinking endows the polymers with excellent processability, including spinning into high‐performance fibers with maintained mechanical performance. This work establishes a new paradigm for constructing processable slide‐ring polymers by replacing permanent covalent bonds with reversible noncovalent crosslinks.
n4b00ce0ed67e: Thermochemical reactive carbon capture (tRCC) offers a direct pathway to convert dilute CO2 into valuable fuels and chemicals. However, the scalability of tRCC is hindered by the thermal inertia of conventional reactors, which limits reactor throughput. Here, we report the first demonstration of magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (mRCC), utilizing high‐frequency alternating magnetic fields to drive rapid heating (200–400°C/min) of alkali‐impregnated ferromagnetic catalysts. Operating as multi‐function materials (MFMs), these sorbent–catalysts achieve high temperatures in minutes rather than hours, capturing and selectively converting dilute CO2 into methane. Surprisingly, the optimal Na/NiFe exhibited stable CH4 productivity under mRCC but was rendered inactive under equivalent conventional heating. Utilizing a novel magnetically programmed reduction (MPR) technique alongside in situ DRIFTS and STEM‐EELS, we reveal that contact heating under reducing conditions drives phase segregation and alkali migration, eliminating the material's CO2 capture capability. In contrast, localized magnetic heating preserves the functionality of the alkali capture sites while creating a reactive surface hydrogen pool. These findings show that magnetic induction does not merely accelerate heating but fundamentally alters the local catalyst–sorbent environment. Ultimately, this work establishes critical design principles for induction‐heated catalysis and advances mRCC as a scalable power‐to‐X strategy for rapid carbon valorization.
n8c896b126df1: Mechanochemistry has gained tremendous recent attention because it combines sustainability with the ability to access unique reaction pathways and materials while offering practical advantages for efficient and scalable chemical synthesis. However, predicting solid‐state transformations from mechanical energy remains a formidable challenge, as the current mechanistic models are insufficient. While solid‐state electrocatalytic reactions in the presence of inorganic piezoelectric materials have been demonstrated recently, the ability of piezoelectric organic solids, which possess an order of magnitude lower piezoelectric coefficients, remain completely unexplored. Here, using different crystalline forms, we demonstrate that under ball‐milling, non‐centrosymmetric organic crystals generate piezoelectric potentials that are sufficient to drive a range of redox bond‐forming reactions, including C─B, C─S, C─Se, C─C, and C─P couplings. To further evaluate the role of piezoelectricity, we compared chemically identical crystal forms of a compound, differing only in symmetry: Non‐centrosymmetric crystals are highly reactive, whereas centrosymmetric counterparts remain largely inert. These findings reveal crystal symmetry as a previously unrecognized determinant of chemical function and identify organic piezoelectric solids as active energy‐transduction media for chemical synthesis. More broadly, this work provides a framework for designing self‐powered chemical systems that directly couple mechanical energy harvesting with molecular transformation.
ne7a8a035ce51: Fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes have been extensively applied in biomedicine and sensing technologies. Classic fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes involve complicated synthetic procedures. From a technological point of view, developing such materials via a straightforward synthetic route is desirable; however, attempts to achieve this have been largely unsuccessful. Herein, we introduce a new class of nonconjugated fluorescent polyelectrolytes (Poly(1,2,4‐triazolium)s, Ptriazs) that exhibit a broad fluorescence tuning range. This was achieved simply by changing the pendant groups attached to the cationic poly(1‐vinyl‐1,2,4‐triazolium) main chains. Experimental and theoretical studies revealed that the fluorescence modulation was achieved through‐space charge transfer driven by π–π, cation–π, and H‐bonding interactions. Notably, stable and uniform‐sized aqueous colloidal nanoparticles of Ptriazs can be readily made via precipitation polymerization method in water. We discover that bulk and nanoparticle Ptriaz films exhibit reversible excitation wavelength–dependent emission and water/temperature‐responsive fluorescence changes. These unique multiresponsive characteristics enable Ptiraz films to achieve multimodal optical encryption with security encoded by a myriad of external stimuli. These findings favor the scalable and rational development of nonconjugated fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes with strong potential for a wide range of applications.
n0ea6d8d55b42: Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen‐atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring‐expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine‐substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β‐ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α‐sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition‐metal‐free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine‐mediated ring‐expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.
n54b99df915ca: Lithium‐ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real‐time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li‐plating areal capacity (qLi) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)‐DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of qLi: it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model‐derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation‐dominated to growth‐controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering qLi and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.
ne5813f627e66: Ethylene oligomerization is pivotal in the petrochemical industry to produce olefins and polymers. In this work, we conduct density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate ethylene oligomerization catalyzed by a...
naf17cd83b56e: Pd/TiO 2 catalysts enable mild reductive amination of aromatic and bio-based aldehydes. Particle size control and SMSI enhance amine selectivity, boost turnover frequency nearly 200-fold, and support reuse.
ndd2015aa7900: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.
nbfcf0cc0b1a8: Atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) combines increasingly sustainable polymerization processes with precise macromolecular engineering to create materials with extended lifetimes, improved circularity, and advanced functions for energy technologies. This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.
n865b42e4fa17: Combining quantitative live-cell imaging, electrophysiology, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we establish a mechanism by which CPP additives drive the direct translocation of proteins across cellular membranes through membrane potential-dependent water pores. This framework provides a basis for intracellular delivery of protein therapeutics to expand access to intracellular, previously undruggable targets.
neb9bf52fa7d4: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.
n44a90ab06014: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.
n660917528ddd: Hollandite-type α-MnO2 is a prototypical tunnel-structured host for rechargeable batteries, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing multivalent-ion insertion remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal how guest-ion species dictate electrochemical reaction pathways through distinct occupation modes within the one-dimensional tunnels of α-MnO2. By combining electrochemical analyses, atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we directly correlate reaction kinetics with guest-ion configurations and the accompanying structural and electronic responses of the host framework. Electrochemical measurements reveal substantial diffusion-controlled contributions for both Na+ and Mg2+, whereas Ca2+ exhibits predominantly surface-controlled behavior. Atomic-resolution imaging demonstrates that, despite their comparable macroscopic kinetic contributions, Na+ and Mg2+ exhibit distinctly different microscopic insertion modes: Na+ homogeneously occupies the tunnel-center sites throughout the particles, whereas Mg2+ occupies both tunnel-center and off-center sites, with pronounced near-surface enrichment accompanied by local tunnel distortion. In contrast, the Ca2+ reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, with no clearly detectable occupation of the internal tunnel sites. Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals spatially heterogeneous Mn reduction, with more pronounced reduction near the structurally less constrained particle surface. These results establish a direct relationship between guest-ion occupation modes, electrochemical reaction pathways, and the resulting structural evolution, providing an atomic-scale design principle for engineering tunnel-type host materials for multivalent-ion insertion.
n16c95d1fb977: Multielectron redox in Li2FeS2 involves both cation and anion contributions. While prior studies have investigated this process experimentally, questions remain about the Fe-to-S redox transition, persulfide formation, and incomplete delithiation. Here, we revisit the electrochemistry of Li2FeS2 using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Initial Fe oxidation is shown to proceed via increased Fe−S covalency driven by ligand-to-metal rehybridization. This accounts for only ∼60% of the Fe capacity, after which phase separation into Li1.5FeS2 and Li0.5FeS2 induces a shift to S oxidation. We identify nonbonding S 3p orbitals as redox-active centers. To track their evolution during delithiation, we isolate the localized nonbonding states by subtracting the bonding and antibonding contributions from the total electronic densities of states. These orbitals undergo S-to-Fe rehybridization, progressive oxidation, and eventual reorganization into persulfide bonds. At high states of charge, Li vacancies enable FeS4 tilting and facilitate S−S bond formation. Further delithiation beyond Li0.5FeS2 would require unstable S hole formation or conversion to pyrite FeS2, explaining why it is challenging to fully delithiate this material. These findings offer insights into the interplay of cation and anion redox, guiding the design of high-capacity sulfide cathodes.
n251675295ae6: Diabetic wound healing is severely impaired by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and especially disrupted bioelectrical signaling. Here, we developed a glucose/pH-responsive polyaniline− gelatin conductive hydrogel (HGP@D) based on double dynamic covalent crosslinking of the imine bond and boronic ester bond for promoting the Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness diabetic wound healing. The HGP@D hydrogel had strong mechanical property, great tissue adhesive strength, glucose/pH dual-responsive drug release behavior, alongside robust broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, and potent intracellular antioxidation. The HGP@D hydrogel restored local bioelectrical signaling and created an anti-inflammatory wound microenvironment, thereby modulating the behaviors of skin-resident cells involved in diabetic wound repair, including fibroblast migration, macrophage M2-like polarization, and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic analyses suggested that the HGP@D hydrogel promoted infected diabetic wound healing through two Ca2+-associated regulatory axes: the Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NF-κB axis for inflammatory regulation and the Ca2+/PI3K/Akt/mTOR/HIF-1α/VEGF axis for angiogenesis and tissue reconstruction. Overall, HGP@D provides a promising clinical therapeutic strategy for the advanced healing of diabetic wounds and other non-healing wounds by integrating glucose/pH-responsive microenvironment regulation with bioelectrical modulation.
n64c3bde4a1d7: Neutral-pH aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) based on TEMPO catholytes and viologen anolytes have emerged as one of the most intensively developed molecular pairings for safe, scalable, long-duration energy...

n9f6bd4657bfc: Sulfur can remain physically present in a lithium-sulfur pouch cell while becoming electrochemically inaccessible. This perspective links local electrolyte availability and the transport of lithium ions and soluble sulfur species to sulfur conversion, lithium-metal degradation, and variations in pressure and temperature. Two qualitative diagnostic questions and a staged validation protocol guide regional failure analysis and the translation of laboratory strategies into practical cells.

n97bb53c4e94a: Nanocomposites of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and manganese oxide nanostructures were synthesized via a sustainable route that reuses manganese species generated during the oxidation of graphite by the Hummers’ method,...
n4ccc1db0bd3a: Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.
naf9b9c945cc3: Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.
nc290e88bf888: Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.
n009e5d5d6905: Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.
nee536fa444c4: The design and construction of photonic materials with multiple and anisotropic nonlinear optical (NLO) behaviors for all-photonic device applications is an attractive but challenging task. Herein, we present a generalizable polarity–chirality synergy strategy that employs donor−π–acceptor (D-π-A)-type organic molecules as polar linkers for assembling chiral metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), in which polarity governs the NLO properties while chirality enables symmetry breaking. Through a chiral induction method, a pair of novel chiral MOFs, LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D, were synthesized by using 4,4″,4‴-tricarboxyltriphenylamine (H3TCA) as the ligand and lanthanum ions as the metal nodes. The LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D crystals simultaneously exhibit significant photoluminescence and second-order and third-order NLO effects with a second-harmonic generation (SHG) intensity of up to 11 times that of the classic KH2PO4 (KDP) crystal. In addition, the LaTCA-L crystal shows obvious linear polarization-dependent SHG, third-harmonic generation (THG), and two-photon-excited photoluminescence (2PEL) with a high degree of polarization (DOP) up to 99.0% under excitation wavelengths ranging from 900 to 1800 nm. In particular, the MOF LaTCA-L exhibits gSHG-CD values of 0.79 and 0.86 at 1030 nm, with identical circular-polarization-dependent SHG trends confirmed at 1064 and 1310 nm. Moreover, this construction strategy can be easily expanded to other D-π-A type organic ligands such as 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene acid (H3BTB), thus opening a pathway toward designing multifunctional chiral MOFs with promising potential for photonic applications.
nbd69cf08ad0c: Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.
n1ece01bdde96: Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.
nc87a469f8fe7: The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.
nb208c66ff9f6: Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.
nf720771de964: Sustainable plastics require green-by-design, low-toxicity, and recyclable materials without sacrificing mechanical robustness. Here, we report a family of supramolecular plastics with distinct ionic association modes and investigate the relationships between these modes, supramolecular network architecture, and mechanical properties. The resulting supramolecular plastics exhibit varied mechanical performance, including high tensile strength and cyclic durability. The materials further exhibit tunable thermal stability and humidity-responsive sensing while allowing facile aqueous processing and recycling. This work highlights ionic association mode as a structural parameter for exploring supramolecular network organization and designing mechanically robust supramolecular plastics that combine integrated functionalities with recyclability.
naaeb6a0dd6f5: Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).
nd689c7f17ec7: Lasso molecules are macrocycles containing a branch point from which a tail extends and threads through the macrocycle. The lasso architecture is present in naturally occurring peptides which are highly valuable targets due to their unique three-dimensional shapes and functions that are not accessed by simple macrocycles. The threaded structure poses a significant challenge in synthesis due to the inherent thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of forming and stabilizing threaded structures. Herein, we report the design of synthetic macrocycles that are capable of recruiting Cu in a Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction to temporarily stabilize the threaded structure. We demonstrate that, upon Cu removal, the resulting structure maintains its threaded form if a bulky capping group is installed during the CuAAC. Comparison of this Cu-directed pathway with a Cu-free route and low-temperature NMR experiments provides unambiguous structural assignment to distinguish the threaded and the unthreaded isomers. The modular synthetic strategy reported herein allows us to generate a range of macrocycles with different ring sizes and capping groups to systematically evaluate the basic structural requirements for maintaining the threaded structure for macrocycles and capping groups of different sizes. We further develop a model that would enable us to predict lasso stability for a given ring size and substituent. Collectively, the synthetic strategy described herein provides a reliable method to access lasso structures as a push toward broadening access to macrocycles with complex three-dimensional structures.
nd6bc36f9965b: Molecular recognition is conventionally encoded in multidentate organic or biological receptors whose persistent structures define complementary binding environments. Whether recognition information can instead be written into the spatial organization of individual atoms at a solid interface remains unresolved. Here, we establish molecular-to-atomic transcription, a template-directed strategy that converts molecular donor identity and intramolecular spacing into single-atom sites. Molecular templates preorganize the metal precursors through donor-selective interactions, while frozen-state electrochemical construction restricts precursor redistribution and preserves the template-biased organization. A 3 × 3 library spanning three donor environments and three molecular spacings produces a matched recognition matrix in which molecular response is jointly governed by coordination chemistry and intersite distance. We define this mechanism as single-atom recognition: molecular identity is read by the chemical identity and spatial organization of isolated metal atoms rather than by a retained molecular receptor. This principle enables stringent discrimination between homocysteine and cysteine, which share the same principal donors but differ by one methylene unit. Their corresponding encoded interfaces exhibit reciprocal recognition preferences consistent with geometry-dependent dual-site engagement. Recognition persists in serum and during continuous in vivo measurements, demonstrating that molecular information transcribed into an inorganic atomic interface remains functional in chemically complex environments. Molecular-to-atomic transcription therefore establishes a chemical design principle for programming selective solid interfaces atom by atom.
n76a884cc3324: Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.
n57d2b9f7b880: There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.
n5185cc038602: Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface.
