WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) operated under MSPT retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation, whereas devices operated under conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) rapidly degrade during the early stages of operation. Post‐operational analyses further reveal that MSPT preserves the alloyed perovskite phase, whereas MPPT induces pronounced phase segregation. As an operation‐stage strategy that mitigates charge accumulation without altering material composition, MSPT is compatible with existing material approaches and offers a route toward more stable perovskite photovoltaics. These findings provide an operational guideline for stabilizing WBG PSCs and advancing tandem photovoltaic technologies.
ndf35edbb38d0: Perovskite Solar Cells In article number e71358, Mansoo Choi, Yun Seog Lee, Namyoung Ahn, and co‐workers report maximum stability point tracking (MSPT) for wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskite solar cells. Trapped‐charge accumulation is identified as a key factor driving halide segregation during operation. By mitigating charge accumulation, MSPT enables devices to retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation.
nfa893a4d8401: Moist‐electric generators (MEGs) convert ambient humidity into electricity, but their inherently low power output makes outdoor deployment as a general energy source impractical. Indoor environments, where humidity is stable and low‐power electronics demand only microwatt‐to‐milliwatt supplies, present a more realistic opportunity—and wallpaper, with its large continuously exposed surface area and seamless architectural integration, is the most compelling platform to realize it. Here we report the first wallpaper‐type MEG, enabled by a peripheral‐absorption, center‐evaporation architecture that achieves engineered unidirectional moisture transport on a single paper sheet. Glycerol at the periphery captures atmospheric moisture; polyvinylpyrrolidone in the intermediate region acts as a bound‐water sink whose reduced porosity and lowered water activity drive inward transport through Laplace pressure and chemical potential gradients; and a wax‐treated center exploits the phase‐selective behavior of hydrophobic pores—blocking liquid while transmitting vapor—to confine evaporation without a solid seal. A concealed through‐hole interconnection strategy enables modular scaling with no visible wiring. A single unit delivers ∼0.34 V and ∼2.2 µW/cm2 at 80% RH with stable output over 90 min. A 1596‐unit array powers a wireless keyboard and simultaneously reduces indoor humidity from 38% to 32%, transforming passive wall surfaces into self‐powered, climate‐responsive interfaces.
nd6b95a988207: Phosphoric acid (PA)‐related challenges, including PA loss, redistribution, and flooding, critically limit the performance and long‐term durability of high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs) based on PA‐doped membrane electrode assemblies. Although these issues can be partially mitigated using proton‐conducting additives and hydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene, practical commercialization remains impeded by restricted high‐temperature operability and the requirement for high Pt loadings. To address these challenges, here we report a cerium hydrogen phosphate (CeHP)‐integrated multifunctional matrix‐activated electrode (MME) that stabilizes PA‐containing electrode microenvironments and preserve electrochemical pathways under severe high‐temperature operation above 200°C, where acid evaporation, dehydration, and migration become increasingly pronounced. This integrated matrix combines high‐temperature proton‐conduction, radical scavenging, and structural reinforcement of the porous catalyst layer, consequently alleviating the degradation at such high temperature. As a result, the optimized MME delivers a 38% increase in peak power density and a 62% reduction in voltage decay rate at 240°C, while requiring only 40% of the Pt loading of a Celtec commercial HT‐PEMFC electrode (0.4 vs. 1.0 mgPt cm−2 per electrode). These results establish multifunctional catalyst‐layer matrix engineering as an effective strategy for enabling durable, low‐Pt HT‐PEMFC operation in acid‐doped polymer electrochemical systems under harsh high‐temperature conditions.
nc7db0276bca4: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells In article number e71438, Hansung Kim, Katie Heeyum Lim, So Young Lee, and co‐workers introduce a cerium hydrogen phosphate‐integrated multifunctional matrix‐activated electrode that transforms the catalyst‐layer microenvironment in high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The matrix strengthens proton‐conduction networks, suppresses radical‐driven degradation, and fortifies the porous catalyst‐layer architecture, enabling remarkably durable, high‐performance operation at reduced Pt loading.
n91860ca44750: Flexible perovskite solar cells (f-PSCs) are highly susceptible to ultraviolet (UV) degradation and mechanical brittleness during ambient-air fabrication, hindering their commercialization. Herein, we engineer an anti-UV ionic liquid (1-vinyl-3-[3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl]imidazolium chloride, IL-SiO-2) featuring a tailored C═C-imidazolium hybrid architecture to address these challenges. The conjugated C═C bonds effectively enable UV shielding to suppress precursor degradation while retarding PbI2 segregation and I3 − generation in perovskite film, thereby preventing f-PSC device deterioration. Simultaneously, the ionic liquid IL-SiO-2's adaptive molecular structure enhances mechanical compliance, enabling robust integration with flexible substrates under bending stress. Ultimately, IL-SiO-2 synergistically enables UV-resistant fabrication of defect-suppressed perovskite films and stabilized f-PSC in air, reducing Young's modulus to 2.58 GPa and grain boundary density by ∼10%, achieving exceptional mechanical durability with 92% power conversion efficiency (PCE) retention after 3,000 bends at R = 2 mm. Remarkable ambient-air stability and humidity resistance are also attained. The fully air-processed f-PSC delivers a negligible hysteresis (0.004) and retains 80.0 ± 1.1% PCE after 360 h in a damp heat test. This work pioneers a multifunctional ionic liquid strategy to concurrently boost UV tolerance, mechanical resilience, and efficiency of f-PSC, charting new pathways for air-compatible fabrication of durable flexible photovoltaics.
n65e71a81eb70: Studies on halide perovskites for electrocatalysis remain in their infancy, largely limited to preliminary attempts at inducing oxygen atoms and improving stability. A key challenge lies in the lack of effective strategies for controlled oxygen atom introduction. Herein, we design a facile method to generate oxygen atoms in Pd single‐atom‐loaded Cs2SnCl6 (O‐Cs2SnCl6@Pd) by using hydrogen peroxide. Under Xe light irradiation, it exhibits a low overpotential (135 mV at 10 mA cm−2) during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with long stability for 100 h. DFT calculations illustrate that the incorporation of oxygen atoms in O‐Cs2SnCl6@Pd modulates the electronic structure, as evidenced by a lowered overpotential for key intermediate species. This modulation further increases electron density, promoting the adsorption and activation of OER intermediates, as well as enabling the population of a new excited state. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further evidences that O atoms reduce the recombination of electron–hole, thereby significantly facilitating charge‐transfer to active sites that promote electrocatalytic reactions. This study introduces a novel strategy for the rational design and synthesis of high‐performance photo‐assisted electrocatalytic materials, offering a pathway to enhanced catalytic efficiency and functionality.
nd57c88fc7c50: Solid oxide cells (SOCs) operate at high temperature under dual atmospheres and electrochemical polarization. Their performance depends not only on composition and instantaneous operating conditions, but also on operating history, because defect populations, transport pathways, and microstructures evolve during service. This behavior limits conventional machine‐learning models trained on static or steady‐state data, because high interpolation accuracy rarely guarantees reliable extrapolation to operando or aging conditions. In this review, physics‐informed machine learning (PIML) encompasses physical knowledge introduced through descriptors, model architectures, generative constraints, and experimental feedback, rather than only neural networks constrained by partial differential equations. We organize representative SOC studies using a four‐level hierarchy of physics embedding and relate it to data fidelity, while tracing descriptors from elemental attributes to dynamic operando‐state variables. We then examine how connectivity, conservation laws, and thermodynamic stability can constrain microstructure inverse design and reject physically inadmissible outputs. Further progress requires closer links among defect chemistry, microstructure physics, service‐relevant data, and experimental feedback, enabling models that remain valid under realistic conditions and support closed‐loop design.
n8676556de9e5: The irreversible consumption of sodium ions during the initial cycle, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity decay, poses a fundamental bottleneck to the commercialization of sodium‐ion batteries. While pre‐sodiation has emerged as a pivotal strategy to compensate for this sodium deficit, the field currently lacks a systematic methodology to critically assess and rationally select among diverse pre‐sodiation tactics beyond mere electrochemical metrics. This review addresses this need by synthesizing existing evaluation criteria into a structured multidimensional assessment paradigm. We first delineate the mechanistic underpinnings of physical, electrochemical, chemical, and additive‐based pre‐sodiation strategies. We then introduce a systematic framework that integrates electrochemical performance, interfacial physicochemical properties, and electrode structural evolution to provide a holistic assessment of pre‐sodiation efficacy. Furthermore, we highlight how advanced operando and ex situ characterization techniques decode underlying compensation mechanisms and quantify kinetic improvements. Finally, a comparative analysis based on controllability, scalability, and manufacturing compatibility is presented, offering strategic guidelines for protocol selection. Ultimately, this work provides a foundational reference and a practical decision‐making guide, facilitating the rational design of efficient pre‐sodiation technologies for practical sodium‐ion batteries.
n92490e49c901: For practical water electrolysis, electrocatalysts must deliver both high activity and stability. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a programmable platform for constructing tailored active sites and coordination environments, offering considerable potential for high activity. However, MOF electrocatalysts typically undergo activation‐induced reconstruction, during which their ordered frameworks transform into disordered active states, generating reconstruction‐induced strain. Poor accommodation of this strain can lead to morphological collapse, metal‐site leaching, and ultimately compromised stability. To address these issues, we leveraged the programmability of MOFs to restrict the long‐range extension of their secondary building units, thereby pre‐introducing disorder into the framework to facilitate strain accommodation during reconstruction. Consequently, activation increased the electrochemically active surface area of the disordered structure, in contrast to the decrease observed for the ordered counterpart, suggesting that destructive reconstruction was effectively mitigated. The resulting active phase retained M–O–M bridging vibrational features even at 1.9 V (vs. RHE), whereas the corresponding features in the ordered MOF were markedly weakened at 1.4 V (vs. RHE), indicating better structural integrity after reconstruction. These advantages enabled stable operation for up to 500 h in an electrolyzer and 1500 h at 1 A cm−2 in a two‐electrode cell, demonstrating excellent durability for overall water splitting.
n9b520ce07922: Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are essential in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) due to superior electrical properties, yet their inherent rigidity imposes severe mechanical stress on the perovskite layer. Herein, we construct an interfacial architecture featuring discontinuous metal‐oxide islands to circumvent this fundamental electro‐mechanical trade‐off at the buried contact. Specifically, this discontinuous topography imparts macroscopic structural flexibility to the interface by functioning as localized strain‑relaxation zones, enabling strain‐relaxed perovskite films with reduced defect density. Meanwhile, the modified interface maintains unimpeded hole‐selective pathways and optimal energy level alignment. Consequently, the corresponding PSC yields a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.92% (certified 26.60%) with enhanced long‐term stability. This strategy establishes a rational design principle for synergistic electro‐mechanical management, paving the way for high‐efficiency and stable photovoltaic devices.
n35a385b60d79: The practical application of perovskite solar cells (PerSCs) is still limited by their intrinsic instability, particularly under dynamic temperature fluctuations in outdoor conditions. In this study, we present a series of dual cross‐linking agents to improve the efficiency and temperature endurance of PerSCs. Specifically, 3‐(trichlorosilyl)propyl methacrylate (MPTCl) with multiple functional groups is applied to modify the upper interface of the perovskite. The ─C═O group exhibits strong interactions with the undercoordinated Pb2+ on the perovskite surface, helping to stabilize structures and reduce interfacial charge recombination. The C═C bond of the methacrylate group undergoes in situ polymerization/cross‐linking, while the trichlorosilyl group undergoes hydrolysis and subsequent condensation under humid conditions, enabling MPTCl to form a Si─O─Si cross‐linked network. This cross‐linked interfacial layer improves interfacial structural stability and enhances resistance to moisture‐ and heat‐induced degradation. Consequently, the optimal PerSCs achieved a high power conversion efficiency of 26.22% and demonstrated enhanced thermal durability under simulated thermal cycling conditions, retaining 82.4% of their initial efficiency after 250 cycles. This work proposes a dual cross‐linking strategy that provides an effective route for simultaneously improving the efficiency and thermal resilience of PerSCs, offering valuable insights into the development of durable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.
nb33b50194617: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) suffer from severe H2O‐induced parasitic reactions and uneven Zn deposition, especially at sub‐zero temperatures. Herein, we propose a hydrated eutectic high‐entropy electrolyte based on Zn(ClO4)2, ethylene glycol, 1,5‐pentanediol, and H2O, which couples a configurationally diverse bulk solvation environment with spatially differentiated interfacial regulation through synergistic enthalpy–entropy effects. Diversified solvation configurations promote the formation of an organic‐rich gradient hybrid solid electrolyte interphase, while enriched dipole–dipole interactions suppress H2O activity and strengthened ion‐dipole interactions provide kinetic buffering for Zn2+ supply. Such coupled solvation and interfacial regulation enables interfacial deposition kinetics to be balanced with bulk ion migration, thereby homogenizing interfacial Zn2+ flux, alleviating concentration polarization, and inhibiting dendritic growth. Moreover, preferential interfacial adsorption of organic species promotes the exposure of the Zn(002) plane, inducing thermodynamically favorable Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells operate for over 2000 h at 25°C and over 3000 h at −20°C. Zn||PANI pouch cells achieve capacity retentions of 91.32% after 1200 cycles at 25°C and 98.65% after 2000 cycles at −20°C, while full cells cycle stably for 500 cycles at −50°C with negligible capacity decay. These findings highlight synergistic enthalpic‐entropic regulation as an effective strategy for developing durable wide‐temperature AZIBs.
n2123105c646c: Thermal runaway has constrained the application of high‑energy‑density batteries. Metalized plastic current collectors (MPCCs) offer a promising approach to reducing inactive mass and improving mechanical safety, yet they remain intrinsically passive and provide no active response to thermal abuse. Here, we propose tunneling‑gated thermoresponsive MPCCs (TTMP), which transforms conventional MPCCs from passive conductors into autonomous, self‑protecting components. The TTMP integrates a polyethylene matrix and embedded spiky carbon conductive particles, sandwiched between ultrathin aluminum layers on both surfaces. Upon heating above 100°C, thermal expansion of the polymer disrupts electron tunneling between adjacent spiky carbon particles, sharply suppressing electrical conduction through the TTMP, thereby interrupting current flow and delaying thermally accelerated electrochemical reactions under abuse conditions. When returns to room temperature, electron transport is fully restored, and the battery resumes normal operation. During thermal triggering, the resistance of the TTMP increases from 6.3 Ω to 2.1 × 105 Ω within a response time of 4 s. Cells equipped with this collector show a reversible reduction in discharge current of up to 92.5%. Furthermore, 1 Ah pouch cells achieve up to 6 cycles of reversible thermal shutdown with complete performance recovery, while the onset of thermal runaway is delayed by up to 30°C.
n76faf9e14fda: Electrochemical CO2 conversion in acid can, in principle, maximize carbon efficiency but is typically undermined by facile hydrogen evolution. Moreover, operating at high current density often triggers a sharp local pH increase that propagates into the bulk electrolyte, causing an overall pH shift that erodes nominally “acidic CO2 reduction” toward neutral/alkaline conditions. To address these limitations, we incorporated Ce species with high proton affinity into the surface of porous Cu nanosheet, constructing proton‐mitigating Cu─O─Ce active sites. Beyond conventional C─C coupling driven by local *CO accumulation, Cu─O─Ce motifs accelerate *CO formation and its protonation, thereby enabling downhill proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) toward and beyond *CO─*CHO dimerization. This strategy demonstrates efficient multi‐carbon generation under retentive pH conditions minimizing the collateral deficiencies of acidic CO2 reduction. Facilitating kinetically suppressed C─C coupling at a relatively low current density offers a strategic catalyst design that maintains a stable bulk pH compared to high current density operations, thereby maximizing the in situ generation of CO2 within the acidic media.
na883ee93c774: Inhomogeneous lithium nucleation at the current collector‐solid electrolyte interface leads to unstable lithium growth and poor reversibility in “lithium‐free” solid‐state batteries. Here we show that stable lithium formation occurs within a mixed ionic and electronic conducting (MIEC) garnet scaffold. The intrinsic electronic conductivity of the porous framework enables lithium to nucleate uniformly along internal pore surfaces, rapidly forming a conformal lithium coating, thus establishing electronic connectivity at very low lithium volume fraction. This uniform lithium formation dramatically lowers anode impedance, enabling reversible lithium plating and stripping with Coulombic efficiencies of a previously unheard‐of 99.95%. When paired with NMC811 cathodes, bilayer (MIEC(P)‐LLZ(D)) “lithium‐free” full cells exhibit stable, highly reversible cycling at practical current densities, all at room temperature with no applied pressure. The interplay between lithium volume fraction and impedance is quantitatively modeled, transforming the understanding of lithium nucleation in a “lithium‐free” cell from an empirical interface problem to a percolation‐governed transport process, guiding the design of electronically percolating scaffolds for next‐generation solid‐state batteries.
n0e20f3b5d1a2: Incorporating dynamic covalent bonds into polymer networks could offer stimuli‐responsive control over molecular transport, often requiring additives to facilitate bond rearrangement. Here super‐resolution localization microscopy was employed to examine fluorescent probe transport in unhydrated, elastic networks containing thiol‐thioester dynamic covalent chemistry (DCC). In static, DCC‐free networks, displacement distributions revealed frequent trapping and slow, anomalous, and heterogeneous diffusion. Introducing a dynamic catalyst additive markedly increased mobile fraction and produced diffusivity that was more fluid‐like. These effects were observed with several classes of fluorescent probes, two distinct additives, and for networks with or without DCC. Experiments with a photo‐releasable catalyst (NPPOC‐TMG) separated additive effects from those of activated exchange. Catalyst release conferred additional fluidization of the network. Importantly, these changes were not accompanied by macroscopic plasticization, suggesting that small additive concentrations can strongly affect transport in confining environments. Spatial analysis further indicated that transport enhancement was primarily due to restructuring of an initially heterogeneous network rather than local bond exchange near the diffusing probes. Additive incorporation and post‐cure exchange likely reduced defects and homogenized the crosslink density. In sum, these results demonstrate how DCC modulates transport, emphasize the importance of the activation method, and highlight its potential in separation and controlled‐release systems.
n424d48f6118c: Control over liquid wettability and droplet mobility is essential for several emerging applications including open microfluidics, anti-icing, self-cleaning, and heat transfer. Existing strategies generally rely on permanent chemical modification or continuous external stimuli to regulate droplet spreading, pinning, and sliding. Here, we report a unified approach for reconfiguring wettability states and droplet mobility by regulating crystalline packing of a semicrystalline polymer. A phase-transitioning polymer, poly(octadecyl acrylate) (PODAc), was incorporated into a porous polymeric coating, where melting and subsequent cooling pathways determine the extent of alkyl-chain crystallization and interfacial polar functionality. Cooling in air or underwater generates reversibly switchable hydrophilic (θ W ∼ 85°), hydrophobic (θ W ∼ 104°), and amphiphobic slippery states across liquids with surface tensions of 22–72 mN m−1. These distinct regimes enable programmable droplet spreading, pinning, and low-friction transport without post-synthetic chemical treatment or sustained external stimulation. Furthermore, reconfigurable wettability patterns enable guided liquid transport through spatially selective complete wetting or customized contact line frictional force.
n13df05101f34: Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two‐dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase‐engineered material platforms.
nf6b471879bff: Organic photodiodes (OPDs) hold significant promise for next‐generation IoT optical sensing and low‐power imaging applications. However, widespread application of OPD in flexible and dynamic imaging has been constrained by high dark current, poor stability, and the lack of a cost‐effective imaging system. In this work, we present an integrated solution through tailoring pseudo‐planar heterojunction (PPHJ) OPD arrays and a customized, rapidly accessible imaging system, the dynamic organic photonics imaging system (DOIS). The resulting PPHJ OPD exhibited a high responsivity (0.6 A W−1 at 868 nm), low dark current (1.5 × 10−8 A cm−2 at −1 V) and fast response time (480 ns), benefiting from optimal vertical phase separation and donor‐acceptor interface morphology. Moreover, flexible photodetector exhibits superior mechanical stability, photostability and storage stability. Crucially, a pixel‐shifting strategy was incorporated into conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) based machine learning algorithms to capture dynamic images and enhance resolution by leveraging sub‐pixel information sampling. This work demonstrates a significant potential for the extensive application of organic photovoltaic materials in image sensing and flexible electronics.
nc45584fb219a: Structural color actuators integrating visual readout with motion are prized for biomimicry, yet typically operate in a coupled, color‐gradient mode with limited freedom. Here we report a photonic liquid crystal network that decouples these responses via a scattering‐gated mechanism. The material hides its structural color in the dry state but, upon water uptake, simultaneously switches on vivid coloration and executes programmable three‐dimensional deformation. Crucially, we achieve stimulus‐selective control: ethanol turns on color without motion, while heat induces motion without color. This independent, on‐demand manipulation of optical and mechanical outputs offers a transformative platform for multi‐responsive soft robotics, adaptive camouflage, and smart displays.
nb2b611c589ad: Lignin‐ based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio‐based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self‐healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.
n57303edc25a9: Dislocations are widely used to tailor lattice thermal conductivity in semiconductors and thermoelectrics, yet the local thermal resistance of individual buried dislocations and their spatial extent remain experimentally unresolved. Here, operando scanning transmission electron microscopy–electron energy-loss spectroscopy thermometry, atomic-resolution imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics are combined to map heat transport across a dislocation array within a 5°SrTiO3 low-angle grain boundary. The effective thermal conductance of the dislocation array is estimated to be ∼35.4 MW m− 2 K− 1 using the bulk reference conductivity, corresponding to a Kapitza length of ∼339 nm. Nanoscale temperature maps reveal a spatially heterogeneous resistance landscape: reconstructed dislocation cores act as sharp thermal bottlenecks over ∼2.14–5.17 nm, with steeper local temperature gradients than inter-core regions, whereas inter-core regions show weaker but more extended modulation over ∼8.34–11.57 nm. Correlative structural and vibrational analyses show that Ti─O bond distortion, Ti valence change, P4 optical-phonon blueshift, and reduced local–bulk phonon density-of-states overlap create a core-specific vibrational environment. These results uncover the underlying mechanism whereby atomic-scale core reconstruction generates nanoscale localized thermal resistance, and offer quantitative descriptors for defect-structure-guided thermal design.
nf4435590c87b: Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) offer a heavy‐metal‐free route to short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetection, but their performance still lags behind lead‐ and mercury‐based CQD systems, and the surface chemistry that limits their performance is not well understood. Here, we identify two independent oxide‐derived trap pathways on the polar terminations of zincblende InSb: oxidation of the In‐terminated {111}A and Sb‐terminated {111}B facets creates chemically distinct mid‐gap states, each of which degrades carrier transport. Density functional theory calculations show that metal halides bind strongly to Sb‐terminated facets, but weakly to In‐terminated facets, while thiolates show the opposite preference; this asymmetry leaves single‐ligand passivation incomplete. Exploiting this orthogonality, we develop a facet‐specific exchange that passivates both terminations and removes their surface oxides in a single step. The resulting CQD films show a fivefold reduction in hole‐trap density and a sixfold improvement in hole mobility relative to thiol‐only controls. The photodetectors achieve 50% external quantum efficiency under 1 V reverse bias at 1390 nm, to the best of our knowledge, the highest reported for InSb CQD photodetectors in the 1300–1500 nm range, along with a 580 ns fall time and 95% photocurrent retention after 100 h of continuous operation.
nf9c28c0dfaf4: Sustainable photonics aims to replace conventional optical materials with environmentally benign alternatives, yet its development is fundamentally constrained by the narrow intrinsic refractive‐index variability of biopolymers. Here we show that a dense–porous periodic architecture yields nearly perfect optical reflection using only polysaccharides. By exploiting the difference in skeletal rigidity between amorphous pectin and crystalline cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), we form alternating dense, high‐refractive‐index pectin layers and porous, low‐refractive‐index CNF layers through a combination of electrodeposition with solvent exchange. This dense–porous periodic architecture yields reflectivities exceeding 97% in the visible range and 95% in the near‐infrared—a range unprecedented for biopolymer‐based optical materials. Moreover, the strategy is simple, scalable, and highly versatile, enabling free spectral design across the visible and near‐infrared regions, broadband metallic‐like reflection, and planar patterning within a single fabrication process. Combined with the low thermal conductivity arising from porous layers and the coexistence of visible transparency and near‐infrared reflection, the resulting films show potential as transparent thermal‐management materials. This work establishes a new materials design principle for biodegradable, polysaccharide‐based photonic systems and advances the field of sustainable photonics.
n7048a8a32c24: Fe/Co bimetallic regulation enables high‐performance microwave absorbers, yet the role of intrinsic coordination disparity in precursor conversion, nonequilibrium phase evolution, and cross‐band loss redistribution remains unclear. We design a poly(arylene sulfide sulfone) (PASS)‐predefined O/S heterogeneous donor‐field strategy to direct competitive–cooperative nonequilibrium phase evolution in Fe/Co systems. Covalently embedded sulfone‐O and thioether‐S sites, with PASS's rigid backbone, create a molecularly preorganized donor field that amplifies non‐equivalent Fe/Co coordination, promoting competitive bonding, differentiated phase pathways, and electronic‐state reconstruction during confined pyrolysis. Fe/Co regulation thus reshapes local phases, O/S chemical environments, and interfacial charge states via Fe─O/Co─S coordination preferences, generating multiphase heterostructures, amorphous/crystalline interfaces, defects, and lattice strain while balancing dielectric polarization, conductive transport, magnetic response, and impedance matching. The resulting CFC absorber achieves cross‐band absorption in low‐frequency 5G and high‐frequency radar bands. CFC‐4 exhibits −73.83 dB at 6.23 GHz (3.20 mm) and −76.59 dB at 16.98 GHz (1.31 mm), with a maximum EAB of 5.03 GHz. CFC‐4∼6 (1–5 mm) show >90% cumulative effective absorption over 2–18 GHz. Finite‐element simulations reveal a maximum RCS reduction of 42.5 dB on PEC. This work establishes O/S donor‐field engineering as a viable route to amplify Fe/Co coordination differentiation for efficient cross‐band microwave absorption.
nae594d0ece54: Hyperbolic polaritons offer a promising approach for subwavelength light confinement and manipulation. While extensively explored across mid‐infrared to terahertz bands, achieving long‐distance focusing at visible frequencies remains challenging due to the trade‐off between long propagation and strong compression. In this work, we demonstrate planar focusing of anisotropic plasmon polaritons with an extended focal length in a MoOCl2/Au heterostructure. By integrating an Au metastructure with the natural hyperbolic material MoOCl2, we convert surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) into surface plasmon hyperbolic polaritons (SPHPs), enabling excitation and focusing of the low‐momentum hybrid anisotropic polariton in the heterostructure. Furthermore, by optimizing the thickness of the MoOCl2 layer, we synergistically enhance both the propagation distance and the field compression. Using transmission‐mode scanning near‐field optical microscopy (SNOM) and quantitative methods, we demonstrate a focal length of 2.5λ and a focal spot with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of λ/5 under 633 nm excitation, accompanied by a threefold energy enhancement. This visible‐frequency long‐focus system offers significant potential for noncontact nanoscale probing, integrated photonics, and optical interconnects. The proposed heterostructure engineering approach provides a versatile design paradigm for coupling hyperbolic polaritons with multiple plasmonic excitations, paving the way for advanced photonic applications.
n073a4618c299: Carbon neutrality demands materials that deliver both performance and low environmental impact. Carbon fiber and glass fiber rely on fossil feedstocks and energy‐intensive processing, while nature bamboo the ecological marvel is limited by inefficient load transfer within their heterogeneous cell walls. Here we show that this limitation can be overcome by reprogramming the bamboo cell wall through supramolecular nano‐reinforcement. Cellulose nanocrystals infiltrate the cell wall and promote the reorganization of the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network within the aligned cellulose framework converting structural discontinuities into a continuous load‐bearing scaffold. This enhances interfibrillar stress transfer and homogenizes mechanical response across scales. The resulting material achieves a tensile strength of 0.98 GPa and a Young's modulus of 52.7 GPa, with specific strength rivaling many synthetic fiber materials. These gains are achieved with up to two orders of magnitude lower carbon intensity than that of carbon fiber. This work demonstrates a scalable route to transform abundant biomass into high‐performance structural materials, decoupling mechanical performance from carbon intensity.
n6bf6e78631f7: Achieving efficient charge transport while maintaining low nonradiative energy loss remains a key challenge in the molecular design of small-molecule acceptors (SMAs) for organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a stepwise molecular engineering strategy based on sulfur locking and chlorination to regulate intermolecular packing and excited-state properties simultaneously. Sulfur locking modifies molecular conformation and intermolecular packing, leading to enhanced exciton diffusion and charge transport. Subsequent chlorination further strengthens intermolecular interactions through additional Cl···S contacts, resulting in tighter π–π stacking and improved crystalline ordering. Binary OSCs based on D18:Qx2Ph-SCl achieve an efficiency of 20.0% with a high open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.951 V, while maintaining a low nonradiative energy loss of ∼0.19 eV. Owing to its intrinsically lower reorganization energy and weaker electron–phonon coupling than L8-BO, Qx2Ph-SCl further serves as an effective third component in ternary OSCs, reducing nonradiative recombination and increasing the V OC. As a result, the ternary device delivers an efficiency of 21.3%. This work demonstrates that stepwise sulfur locking and chlorination provide an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously optimizing charge transport and voltage loss in high-performance OSCs.
nf0811099d9b5: Current periodontitis management is hindered by the inability to effectively reverse the dysbiotic microenvironment of persistent infection and restore immune homeostasis. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) presents a promising non‐invasive antibacterial strategy, its clinical efficacy remains limited by poor microenvironmental selectivity and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Herein, we engineer a microenvironment‐responsive “trash‐to‐treasure” PDT strategy based on Bi2O2CO3 nanosheet‐assembled microspheres. This platform actively scavenges excess hydrogen sulfide (H2S) within the periodontal pocket, triggering an in situ transformation into Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 heterojunctions. This H2S‐triggered conversion neutralizes the pro‐inflammatory gasotransmitter and establishes an S‐scheme heterojunction with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The resulting reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative stress, together with targeted disruption of bacterial iron metabolism, enables highly efficient photodynamic eradication of major periodontopathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis. Moreover, Bi2O2CO3‐mediated scavenging of pathological H2S alleviates inflammatory responses in human gingival fibroblasts and reactivates macrophage respiratory burst for intracellular bacterial clearance. In vivo evaluations in a rat periodontitis model demonstrate effective inflammation resolution, suppression of alveolar bone loss, and robust tissue regeneration. This work introduces an intelligent therapeutic strategy that hijacks pathological H2S as a photodynamic amplifier, establishing a microenvironment‐adaptive PDT paradigm for periodontal infection.
n343f8fc87108: Mechanoluminescent (ML) materials convert mechanical stimuli into light through carrier excitation and radiative recombination, enabling external‐power‐free stress sensing and visualization. The strict energy matching required for carrier release, transport, and recombination restricts ML to narrow thermal windows. Their application at extreme temperatures, however, is constrained by discrete defect levels arising from relatively uniform local atomic environments. Here, we use intrinsic lattice disorder to engineer a quasi‐continuous trap landscape in Sr3Gd2(Ge3O9)2:Mn2+. Diverse local crystal‐field environments, together with dynamically generated defects, create energetically adjacent traps that support a trap‐relay process. Charge carriers are continuously redistributed across this trap manifold, sustaining stable ML over an ultrabroad temperature range from 133 to 433 K. We further demonstrate a human‐machine interaction system based on this material under simulated extreme‐temperature conditions. These results establish intrinsic lattice disorder as a strategy for broadening the thermal operating window of ML materials and provide a general design principle for thermally robust, energy‐storing luminescent materials for extreme environments.
ne09f558187e4: Aluminum (Al) current collectors are crucial for sodium metal batteries (SMBs), yet sodium (Na) dendrite suppression and uniform Na deposition remain challenges. Surface modification could significantly optimize Na deposition behavior. Herein, a 20 nm copper (Cu) layer is designed to confine NiY diatomic catalyst (DAC) for Al surface modification via magnetron sputtering and heat treatment. The adjacent NiY atoms, with low single‐point energy (–228.05 eV), minimum segregation energy (−0.67 eV), and maximum aggregation energy (5.84 eV), synergistically stabilize diatomic dispersion in the Cu nanolayer. Benefiting from the tailored acetylene adsorption energy (−1.16 eV) and favorable formation energies of C2H (−13.58 eV) and C2 (−11.44 eV), NiY–DAC exhibits excellent catalytic activity, in‐situ growth ultra‐long helical CNFs 3D‐networks with a thickness of 46.3 µm on Al current collectors, enabling efficient Na storage and remarkable inhibition Na dendrite formation. The modified current collector delivers outstanding electrochemical performance. The coulombic efficiency is up to 99.49% over 3000 h of half‐cells at 1.0 mA cm−2/1.0 mAh cm−2 with a low overpotential (3.1 mV), and the CNFs‐Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 full‐cells achieve stable cycling over 1500 cycles at 10.0 C. This diatomic catalyst confinement strategy provides new insight into designing high‐performance carbon‐modified current collectors.
n1db4dbb85767: The development of efficient and safe solid‐state hydrogen storage technologies is pivotal for the transition toward sustainable clean energy. Magnesium is a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high gravimetric (7.6 wt.% for MgH2) and volumetric storage capacity (110 kg m−3), abundance, and excellent reversibility. However, the practical application of Mg‐based materials is hindered by their high thermodynamic stability (ΔH = −74.7 kJ mol−1 H2) and sluggish sorption kinetics. Here, we overview the latest advances in Mg‐based composites for high hydrogen storage performance. We discuss key material modification strategies, including catalysis, nanostructuring, alloying, and external field assistance to tune the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of Mg‐based materials. We stress the emerging role of machine learning in accelerating material design, performance prediction, and optimization. We also critically assess the techno‐economic viability of Mg‐based hydrogen storage within integrated hydrogen value chains. This assessment considers how storage connects with hydrogen production, transport, and end‐use applications. Finally, we outline challenges and future research directions, aiming to guide the rational design of next‐generation Mg‐based hydrogen storage materials and systems toward commercial applications.

n4051198ef524: Electrospinning produces lightweight, breathable fiber networks that can reflect sunlight and radiate heat without electricity. As these materials move toward practical use, this review examines how materials chemistry and fiber architecture influence cooling performance. It assesses the strengths and trade-offs of current designs, offering guidance on how to integrate passive cooling into materials that also meet the needs of comfort, moisture transport, and thermal regulation.
nf1d28800f1e1: This work proposes a configurational-entropy strategy to optimize the phase distribution of Dion-Jacobson 2D perovskite indoor photovoltaics. n87284de32f73: Carbon-based nanozymes are expected to reach the catalytic performance of natural enzymes, but their multiparameter synthesis resists rational design. We combined a deep neural network trained on 59 formulations with a differential evolution search algorithm to predict a synthetic route outside the training space, and the measured mass-normalized efficiency matched the prediction. The optimized VS-1 showed a particle size of 2.2 nm, with Fe atoms dispersed and coordinated to approximately 7–8 light atoms (N/O). The optimized VS-1 exhibits a Michaelis constant (Km) of 0.149 mM and a maximum reaction velocity of 2.67 × 10–6 M s–1, demonstrating a substrate affinity approximately three times higher than that of natural horseradish peroxidase. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations based primarily on electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, supported by radical-scavenger trends, identify the superoxide anion radical as the dominant reactive species for substrate oxidation. This work provides a highly active carbon-based catalytic carbon dot for sensing.
nb8cb7826bb18: State-of-charge (SOC) is a central parameter in battery management systems for electric vehicles, directly affecting driving range, power delivery, safety, and battery lifetime. However, real-time and high-precision SOC monitoring remains a challenge for practical batteries. Here, we report a capacity and electrochromism decoupling strategy for real-time SOC monitoring of high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. The bilayer cathode combines a pure electrochromic coloration layer with an underlying conductive, high-loading capacity layer, thereby spatially separating optical readout from high-capacity storage. The device delivers an areal capacity of 3.4 mAh cm–2 with 97.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The monotonic SOC–Hue relationship with 1% SOC intervals was established by converting in situ reflectance spectra into Hue values. The modulation of reflectance-peak wavelength shift retains 81.2% after 1000 coloration cycles. This architecture provides a route toward batteries with built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.
n1a2e830dcba4: The Casimir effect, where conducting plates restrict electromagnetic vacuum modes, is a cornerstone of quantum field theory but has no known analogue in semiconductor excitonic systems. Here we report a Casimir-like excitonic state in twin-structured type-II core/shell quantum dots, where the two-core geometry analogously suppresses hole wave functions. Using a finite-difference effective-mass framework, we identify three excitonic states in CdS/ZnSe quantum dots: a weakly confined state, a Casimir-like state in which the intercore gap suppresses the hole wave function by analogy with conducting plates in the Casimir effect, and a bonding state with intercore hole delocalization. Energy-distance analysis reveals a characteristic intercore gap where the Casimir-like force vanishes, marking the attractive-repulsive transition. The exciton binding energy remains nearly invariant across all three states, contrasting with single-core QDs where it varies streriously. These results establish intercore geometry as an effective degree of freedom for exciton engineering in multicore quantum dot architectures.
n48b394b4e712: Nanoparticle-based combination therapy suffers poor spatiotemporal coordination from mismatched drug release. Herein, we report a poly(l-glutamic acid) (PLG) nanosystem that exploits distinct ester hydrolysis kinetics of a vascular-disrupting agent (combretastatin A4, CA4) and a hypoxia-responsive prodrug (imidazoquinoline azide, IMDQ-N3) for spatiotemporal coordination, while incorporating antigen-capturing moieties to enhance immune responses. Importantly, to overcome the limitations of conventional labeling methods, which only track the nanocarrier backbone and are prone to false-positive results, we developed a label-free, dual-extraction LC-MS/MS workflow to distinguish free from conjugated drugs, revealing the in vivo fate and providing direct quantitative validation of our kinetic design at the drug level. Our results show that free drugs accounted for only 4.6% and 0.2% of total circulating drugs, markedly reducing toxicity. The optimized formulation achieved spatiotemporally coordinated differential release and activation within tumors. This synergistic kinetic design and novel analytics provide a design paradigm and validation tool for PLG-based combination therapy.
n01083b68649e: Coupled Chern layers can realize axion insulators, but topological gap retention and spin-selective hinge control remain material challenges. We propose a material-design strategy using inversion-symmetric half-Chern layers, exemplified by an antiferromagnetic Ni2I2 stack. Opposite odd-Chern layers at inequivalent inversion embeddings fix an axionic decoupled reference. Interlayer-centered parity–time symmetry and half-Chern spin selectivity help retain the layer-derived gap upon coupling. First-principles calculations predict an axion insulator with a 163 meV bulk gap. A material-informed model shows how interlayer coupling gaps the Chern-layer edge-state manifold, leaving termination-dependent chiral hinge channels. Reversing transverse canting relocates a hinge channel and reverses its propagation while retaining the dominant longitudinal-spin sign inherited from its terminal layer. Layer parity selects relative hinge arrangements and spin sectors, enabling coordinated control of position, chirality, and longitudinal spin.
ned06259f57fc: While sonodynamic therapy (SDT) holds promise for localized tumor ablation, its ability to elicit systemic antitumor immunity remains inadequate due to weak immunogenic priming. Herein, we report a dual-engine single-atom-engineered nanoplatform (MNSe) that converts SDT into a robust immunological reprogrammer via irreversible mitochondrial sabotage. By tuning the central heteroatom of an isoindigo derivative, selenium substitution significantly amplifies spin–orbit coupling, maximizing ultrasound-triggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Conjugation with a triphenylphosphonium moiety precisely localizes this amplified oxidative stress to mitochondria. Rationally coupling atom-enhanced ROS with precise subcellular targeting effectively exceeds the biological damage threshold and overcomes endogenous repair mechanisms. The resulting organelle disruption triggers substantial cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA to robustly activate the cGAS-STING pathway. In vivo, this drives interferon-β secretion and CD8+ T-cell infiltration to inhibit primary and distant tumors and to establish durable immunological memory against tumor recurrence, providing a powerful paradigm for spatiotemporally controllable cancer immunotherapy.

n27e93fa2b723: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface. The results show that hydrated Na+ promotes cathodic interfacial mass accumulation, forming a cation-bridged microenvironment that enriches alkynol and limits H2 availability. Positive polarization disrupts this microenvironment, promotes product removal, and restores surface hydrogen. Based on these results, we developed an oscillating potential program (100 s at –0.9 V, 20 s at +0.5 V) to control reactant enrichment, product removal, and hydrogen availability, increasing alkenol selectivity from ∼50% to 97% while enhancing activity by 173%.
nb06f4a8a76c1: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.
n58d4fa2c7544: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements. The transient geometries and electronic properties of liquid atoms within a dynamic matrix increase the possibility to align with various reactants, enabling energy-favorable adsorption patterns and reaction pathways. The catalytic properties of liquid media can be tuned by regulating the dissolved components and/or combining with other functional species. To date, a variety of bond dissociation and formation reactions, centering on C–C, C–H, C–O, C=C, C–N, and C–Cl, have been achieved using liquid metal media. The distinctive catalytic phenomena and the underlying mechanisms associated with liquid metals challenge the conventional understanding of catalysis based on solid-state catalysts. The use of liquid metal media for chemical reactions remains at an early stage, offering great opportunities for future exploration.
nb567c17ed8b9: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3. By hydrothermally tailoring AlOOH precursors and exploiting a topotactic phase transition, three γ-Al2O3 supports (Al2O3-AIP, Al2O3-NP, and Al2O3-NF) with distinct distributions of terminal μ1-OH and doubly bridged μ2-OH sites were prepared. Systematic characterization showed that the hydroxyl-rich Al2O3-NP and Al2O3-NF supports produced substantially smaller Pt–Sn particles than Al2O3-AIP. Spectroscopic trends suggest preferential involvement of acidic μ1-OH sites at lower precursor loadings and progressively greater involvement of μ2-OH sites as the μ1-OH sites approached saturation. The μ2-OH-enriched surfaces favored precursor anchoring associated with highly dispersed Pt–Sn clusters (∼0.6 nm) after reduction. In propane dehydrogenation at 580 °C, the μ2-OH-enriched 0.5Pt–1.3Sn/Al2O3-NF catalyst achieved an initial propane conversion of 60% while maintaining a propylene selectivity above 97%. Site-occupancy experiments and C3H6-DRIFTS further suggest that precursor anchoring involving μ2-OH sites is associated with improved Pt–Sn dispersion and weaker propylene adsorption. These results show that controlling surface hydroxyl types can regulate metal anchoring and particle growth in Al2O3-supported dehydrogenation catalysts.
nea087f14cc45: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.
n525ad58bd624: Understanding the role of low-valent cobalt species in cross-coupling catalysis remains a central challenge, particularly in distinguishing two-electron organometallic pathways from radical-based mechanisms. Herein, we report the isolation and comprehensive characterization of cobalt(II) and cobalt(I) intermediates supported by a tetradentate diazapyridinophane (tBuN4) ligand and elucidate their roles in Kumada cross-coupling reactions. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal partial ligand-centered reduction in the “Co(I)” species, which function as single-electron initiators for halogen atom transfer from aryl bromides. Mechanistic investigations suggest that the resulting aryl radicals follow two distinct pathways: solvent-mediated hydrogen atom transfer leading to protodehalogenation, or interception by Grignard reagents to form C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds through an SRN1-type mechanism (radical-nucleophilic aromatic substitution). Overall, these findings establish a radical-mediated framework for Co-catalyzed Kumada coupling and highlight ligand denticity as a key factor in governing reaction pathways.
n2342929d41a8: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking. The catalyst comprises highly dispersed rhodium (Rh) species anchored on an amorphous NbOx-doped γ-Al2O3 support. The amorphous Nb–O–Al interfaces generate electron-deficient Nb centers that function as medium-strong Lewis acid sites, while simultaneously modulating the electronic and coordination environment of the adjacent Rh species responsible for H2 activation. The nanoscale proximity of these complementary sites facilitates the coupling of acid-mediated C–C bond transformation with the subsequent hydrogenation of reactive intermediates. When applied to the hydrocracking of low-density polyethylene under mild conditions (240 °C, 2 MPa H2), the optimized Rh/10Nb–Al catalyst achieves a liquid product space-time yield of 283 gliquid·gmetal–1·h–1 with a methane selectivity of only 0.77%. Quantitative analysis reveals a linear correlation between the density of these interfacial strong Lewis acid sites and the hydrocracking activity, thereby directly linking the catalytic performance to the interfacial structure. This study establishes interfacial engineering as a rational strategy to encode metal–acid intimacy into the catalyst architecture, thereby offering a general design principle for selective plastic-to-fuel conversion.
n16220f3a2062: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.
n79d26d1e8ae9: The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.
n929edd1b75c4: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.
nd19a205d0334: Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.
nbb19243ce8a1: Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.
na48a6f98f21f: Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by >3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.
n6f61e75fcb12: Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.
nea9a03d80977: Aquatic foods provide around 15% of consumed animal-derived protein worldwide and aquaculture now supplies most of it. But the industry faces significant challenges in disease prevention and excessive use of antimicrobials. Vaccination, particularly for juvenile fish, can mitigate these risks, but manual and automated needle-based vaccination methods are costly, stressful, and labor-intensive. Here, a water-resistant, food-grade microneedle platform is designed to deliver cargos underwater. Silk fibroin-based microneedles are engineered to remain water resistant from minutes to hours in order to penetrate fish skin in wet conditions. To meet the requirements of different underwater applications, three microneedle morphologies─shell, solid-tip, and hollow─are developed, and their different combinations of mechanical integrity, water-resistance performance, cargo compatibility, and release kinetics are studied. The microneedles also preserve the supercoiled conformation of ⩾50% of the loaded pIHNVw-G plasmids─developed to protect fish against infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus─outside the cold chain for 4 weeks under dry conditions. In pilot animal studies, injected microneedles remain attached to zebrafish and juvenile rainbow trout while swimming. Using this food-based microneedle platform, we envision the development of tools for underwater vaccination of juvenile fish that increase aquaculture efficiencies and reduce environmental impact.
nfdc98ccc5673: When early intermediates begin to bias subsequent pathways during protein self-assembly remains difficult to resolve experimentally because early-stage processes are transient and poorly accessible. Here, using regenerated silk fibroin as a model system, we experimentally capture and analyze an early nucleation window in which assembly pathways begin to diverge before conformational locking occurs. By combining controlled electric-field perturbation with multiscale structural characterization and coarse-grained simulations, we identify reproducible nanoscale intermediates that mediate pathway selection. Within this window, electric fields bias early assembly kinetics in a nonmonotonic manner, modulating the formation, elongation, and competition of intermediates rather than directly enforcing structure or orientation. Time-resolved measurements show that subsequent growth proceeds primarily through elongation and fusion of existing intermediates, while β-sheet formation and crystallization emerge only at later stages and serve to stabilize pathways that were biased at earlier stages. Together, we locate the emergence of detectable pathway biasing within the nucleation stage and provide a framework for understanding and guiding protein self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions.
ne053ce2870b1: Sodium-metal batteries are promising for low-temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME-rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na+ and anions (PF6 −/BF4 −), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE-rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic-rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na+ migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled-up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.
nf4d8d0a9edcb: Residual tumor cells and the immunosuppressive microenvironment caused by incomplete radiofrequency ablation (iRFA) lead to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence. In this study, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel, an injectable sono-piezocatalytic hydrogel, is developed for local treatment of HCC after iRFA. It combines hyaluronic acid-modified, oxygen vacancy-engineered Mn–Ti metal–organic framework nanosheets (HA-V-MTO) with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive liposomes co-loaded with STING agonist MSA-2 and an anti-PD-1 antibody (LMP) within a thermosensitive chitosan/β-glycerophosphate (CS/β-GP) hydrogel. Oxygen-vacancy engineering lowers the O2 adsorption energy from 0.187 to −2.559 eV and raises the piezoelectric coefficient d 33 from 35.36 to 108.73 pm V−1. Under ultrasound, HA-V-MTO generates ROS through sono-piezocatalysis, with an additional Fenton-like reaction from the Mn-containing framework. The resulting oxidative stress induces mitochondrial injury and promotes cytosolic mtDNA release, thereby facilitating cGAS-mediated STING activation. ROS-mediated LMP destabilization releases MSA-2, which further enhances STING signaling. The hydrogel undergoes temperature-triggered gelation for sustained local release. In a post-iRFA model, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel + US raises intratumoral IFN-β 7.9-fold, increases the proportion of mature dendritic cells to 50.8% and that of intratumoral CD8+ T cells to 26.5%, suppresses residual regrowth, prolongs survival, and protects against tumor rechallenge. This work presents a locally retained sono-piezocatalytic system that couples tumor killing with STING-driven immune activation after iRFA.
ne9533fb34810: Spider silk exhibits exceptional mechanical properties, inspiring the development of diverse biomimetic fibers. However, spider silk‐inspired fibers typically introduce β‐sheet‐like domains while neglecting microphase structure regulation, failing to overcome inherent strength‐toughness conflict. Herein, a spider silk‐inspired fiber is fabricated through a microphase engineering strategy by mimicking spidroin assembly process and microphase structure evolution during natural spider silk spinning. Polyurethane (PU) serves as raw material because its molecular structure closely resembles that of nature spidroin's architecture. Through a solvent exchange‐induced phase separation process, the long‐range oriented microphase structures are constructed. The as‐spun fiber achieves a high toughness of 626.14 ± 38.01 MJ m−3, surpassing that of the strongest natural spider silk. Subsequently, post‐treatment is applied to induce crystallization, further increasing the tensile strength to 418.21 ± 9.56 MPa while maintaining a high toughness of 333.09 ± 20.64 MJ m−3. Notably, the spider silk‐inspired fiber can be used as an energy‐absorbing layer in a ballistic board due to its excellent energy dissipation capabilities, reducing deformation by 36.5% compared with a ceramic‐aramid control upon impact with a ∼730 m s−1 bullet. This work highlights the microphase engineering strategy in enhancing mechanical properties of fibers, offering a simple pathway to fabricate high‐performance spider silk‐inspired fibers.
n1b52885c362e: Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC‐derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte‐endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human‐relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3, HEY1, JAG1, and N‐cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)‐dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single‐cell RNA‐sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal‐adhesion components and alterations in Notch‐pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte‐mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.
n70fbb8424e77: Burn treatment remains a tough clinical hurdle, as traditional epidermal growth factor (EGF) treatments suffer from rapid proteolytic degradation and poor skin permeation.
